Detailed description of any protocol deviation that occurred during specimen collection, processing, or handling. Required for regulatory documentation.

The day relative to the reference date (typically first dose or randomization) on which the specimen was collected. Negative values indicate pre-treatment, positive values indicate post-treatment.
The date and time when this biospecimen record was last modified in the system. Supports audit trail and change tracking for regulatory compliance.
The quantity of specimen collected, measured in the unit specified in volume_unit. Used to determine sufficiency for planned assays.

Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Tracks which medicinal product each subject received. Required for product-specific safety reporting (ICH E2A), efficacy analysis by product, and regulatory queries about subject exposure in multi-pro
Reference to the clinical trial subject (patient) record. Links to the subject master record sourced from Medidata Rave EDC.
reference: ICH E6(R2); HIPAA 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164; GDPR Article 9

description: Reference to the specific protocol version under which the subject was enrolled. A trial may have multiple protocol amendments; this captures the version active at enrollment.

Reference to the randomization scheme (schedule) used for this subject's assignment. A trial may use multiple schemes (e.g., by phase, cohort, or amendment). Links to the randomization scheme master record in Medidata Rave RTSM.
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312

description: Reference to the parent clinical trial under which this subject was screened and enrolled. Links to the trial master record in Oracle CTMS.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

description: The ratio of subjects allocated to each treatment arm as defined in the randomization scheme (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1:1:1'). Determines the probability of assignment to each arm. Sourced from the RTSM randomization schedule.
reference: ICH E9 Section 2.3; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Indicates the current blinding state of the subject's treatment assignment. 'blinded' = treatment assignment concealed; 'open_label' = treatment known from outset; 'unblinded' = previously blinded assignment has been revealed. Critical for data integrity and regulatory compliance.
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Blinding

description: The number of subjects per randomization block used in the blocked randomization scheme. Confidential as knowledge of block size could compromise blinding. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM randomization parameters.
reference: ICH E9 Section 2.3; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; FDA Guidance on Randomization

description: Date on which the subject completed all protocol-required study procedures and follow-up visits. Populated only when enrollment_status = completed. Used for study close-out and final analysis datasets.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC CDASH Standard; ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration

description: Timestamp when this enrollment record was first created in the source system (Medidata Rave RTSM or Oracle CTMS). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2) GCP guidelines.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Subject Key
description: The natural/business key for this subject enrollment record as assigned by Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS. Used for cross-system reconciliation between CTMS and Medidata Rave EDC. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

description: Flag indicating whether the subject's enrollment and randomization data has been locked for analysis (database lock). True = data locked and frozen for statistical analysis; False = data still open for query resolution or updates. Critical for regulatory submission readiness.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data; CDISC Standards

description: Flag indicating whether the subject has been confirmed as meeting all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria as defined in the trial protocol. True = eligible; False = not eligible or assessment pending. Drives enrollment decision in RTSM.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria

description: Date on which the subject was formally enrolled into the clinical trial following eligibility confirmation. Represents the principal business event timestamp for the enrollment transaction. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC CDASH Standard

description: Current lifecycle status of the subject within the enrollment and randomization workflow. Drives Intent-to-Treat (ITT), modified ITT, and Per-Protocol (PP) population definitions. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM and Oracle CTMS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screened|screen_failed|enrolled|randomized|withdrawn|completed|discontinued — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312

description: Flag indicating whether a valid, signed Informed Consent Form (ICF) has been confirmed for this subject prior to any study procedures. True = ICF confirmed; False = ICF not confirmed or pending. Mandatory GCP compliance check.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50.25; EMA Regulation (EU) No 536/2014

description: Date on which the subject signed the Informed Consent Form (ICF), confirming voluntary participation in the trial. Must precede any study-specific procedures per GCP requirements. Critical for regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50; EMA Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Article 29; GDPR Article 7

description: Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population. True = subject is part of the ITT population (all randomized subjects regardless of protocol adherence). Drives primary efficacy analysis per ICH E9.
reference: ICH E9 Section 5.2; ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands; 21 CFR Part 314; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

description: Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the modified Intent-to-Treat (mITT) analysis population. Criteria for mITT inclusion are protocol-defined (e.g., received at least one dose). Supports secondary efficacy analyses.
reference: ICH E9 Section 5.2; ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on ITT Principle; 21 CFR Part 314

description: Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the Per-Protocol (PP) analysis population. True = subject completed the trial per protocol without major deviations. Used for sensitivity analyses in NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
reference: ICH E9 Section 5.2; ICH E9(R1); 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Statistical Principles

description: Unique alphanumeric code assigned by the RTSM system at the point of randomization, linking the subject to their treatment arm assignment within the randomization schedule. Confidential during blinded phase; revealed only upon unblinding. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM.
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Date on which the subject was randomized and assigned to a treatment arm via the RTSM system. May differ from enrollment_date in trials with a run-in period. Null for screen-failed or non-randomized subjects.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312

description: The natural/business key for this subject enrollment record as assigned by Medidata Rave EDC/RTSM. Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracing back to the authoritative EDC source system.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

description: Coded or free-text reason why a subject failed screening and was not enrolled. Populated only when enrollment_status = screen_failed. Used for protocol feasibility analysis and site performance monitoring. Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC screen failure CRF.
reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data; CDISC CDASH Standard

description: Date on which the subject first presented at the investigational site for screening assessments. Marks the start of the eligibility evaluation period. Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

description: Unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to a subject at the point of screening, prior to eligibility confirmation. Format is site-specific and assigned sequentially by the RTSM system in Medidata Rave. Used to track screen failures and pre-enrollment activity.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8.3; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

description: Value of the first stratification factor used to balance treatment arm assignments across key prognostic variables (e.g., disease stage, geographic region, biomarker status). Defined in the trial protocol and captured at randomization in RTSM.
reference: ICH E9 Section 2.3; ICH E6(R2); CDISC CDASH Standard

description: Value of the second stratification factor used to balance treatment arm assignments (e.g., prior therapy, performance status, age group). Null if the trial uses fewer than two stratification factors. Captured at randomization in RTSM.
reference: ICH E9 Section 2.3; ICH E6(R2); CDISC CDASH Standard

description: Value of the third stratification factor used to balance treatment arm assignments (e.g., country, mutation status, weight band). Null if the trial uses fewer than three stratification factors. Captured at randomization in RTSM.
reference: ICH E9 Section 2.3; ICH E6(R2); CDISC CDASH Standard

description: Unique identifier assigned to a subject upon successful enrollment into the trial. Typically formatted as site-number-sequential-ID (e.g., 001-001). Assigned by Medidata Rave RTSM upon eligibility confirmation and enrollment confirmation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8.3; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

description: Code identifying the treatment arm (e.g., active drug, placebo, comparator, dose level) to which the subject was assigned at randomization. Confidential in blinded trials. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM randomization schedule.
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2); CDISC CDASH Standard; 21 CFR Part 312

description: Human-readable description of the treatment arm assignment (e.g., 'Drug A 100mg QD', 'Placebo', 'Drug B 200mg BID'). Confidential in blinded trials. Complements treatment_arm_code for reporting and analysis.
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2); CDISC CDASH Standard

description: Date on which the subject's treatment assignment was unblinded. Populated only when blinding_status = unblinded. Emergency unblinding events must be documented per GCP. Null for blinded or open-label subjects.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Blinding; EMA Guideline on Blinding

description: Coded reason for the unblinding of the subject's treatment assignment. Emergency unblinding (e.g., for medical management of a Serious Adverse Event) must be documented and reported per GCP and pharmacovigilance requirements. Null for blinded or open-label subjects.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.13; ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Guideline on Blinding

description: Timestamp when this enrollment record was last modified in the source system. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2). Used for incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

description: Date on which the subject withdrew from the trial or was discontinued. Populated only when enrollment_status = withdrawn. Used for survival analysis (censoring) and dropout rate reporting.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC CDASH Standard

description: Coded or free-text reason for subject withdrawal or discontinuation from the trial (e.g., adverse event, consent withdrawal, lost to follow-up, protocol deviation, investigator decision). Null for active or completed subjects. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: adverse_event|consent_withdrawal|lost_to_follow_up|protocol_deviation|investigator_decision|sponsor_decision|death|other — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH E6(R2); ICH E9; CDISC CDASH Standard; 21 CFR Part 312

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each CRF form definition record in the Medidata Rave electronic data capture system. Primary key for the crf_form data product.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: CRF form design approval requires qualified clinical data manager or medical reviewer signature. Current text field 'approved_by' should be FK to employee for qualification verification and electronic

description: Reference to the clinical trial for which this CRF form definition was designed. Links the instrument definition to its parent study in the CTMS.
Reference to the scheduled or unscheduled visit with which this CRF form is associated in the study schedule of events. Null for common forms appearing across all visits.
reference: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM TV Domain

description: Annotated CRF text describing the SDTM variable mappings, derivation rules, and coding instructions associated with each field on this form. Used by data management and programming teams for SDTM dataset creation.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Current lifecycle approval state of the CRF form definition. 'draft' indicates design in progress; 'under_review' indicates pending sponsor/CRO review; 'approved' indicates GCP-compliant sign-off; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer version; 'retired' indicates no longer in use.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

description: Date and time when this CRF form definition received formal GCP-compliant approval. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Required for audit trail under 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; FDA Guidance on Electronic Records

business_glossary_term: Clinical Data Acquisition Standards Harmonization (CDASH) Domain
description: CDISC CDASH domain code indicating the data collection standard this form adheres to (e.g., 'AE', 'VS', 'CM'). Ensures harmonized data collection aligned with CDASH implementation guides.
reference: CDISC CDASH Implementation Guide v2.0; ICH E6(R2)

description: Detailed instructions for site staff on how to complete this CRF form, including definitions, coding conventions, and data source guidance. Embedded in the EDC and printed CRF booklet.

Specifies whether completion of this CRF form is mandatory for all subjects, optional, or conditional on specific criteria (e.g., only if a prior form field triggers it). Drives data completeness monitoring and query generation.
Date and time when this CRF form definition record was first created in the system. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Required for audit trail under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; GDPR Article 5

description: Specifies the data entry mode configured for this CRF form in Medidata Rave. 'single' requires one entry; 'double' requires independent dual entry for critical data; 'auto' is populated programmatically from device or lab feeds.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Medidata Rave Configuration Guide

description: Total number of programmed edit checks (validation rules) configured for this CRF form in Medidata Rave. Provides a measure of form complexity and data quality control coverage.
reference: CDISC Edit Check Specification; Medidata Rave Study Design

business_glossary_term: Case Report Form (CRF) Effective End Date
description: Date on which this CRF form version was retired or superseded. Null for currently active versions. Supports version lifecycle management and historical data traceability.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

business_glossary_term: Case Report Form (CRF) Effective Start Date
description: Date from which this CRF form version is active and available for data entry at investigational sites. Supports version management and ensures sites use the correct form version.
reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data; Medidata Rave Study Design

description: Total number of data fields (questions/items) defined on this CRF form. Used for form complexity assessment, site burden estimation, and data management planning.
reference: CDISC CDASH; Medidata Rave Study Design Specification

description: Short display label for the CRF form used in the EDC user interface and printed CRF booklets. May differ from form_name for brevity in UI contexts.
reference: CDISC CDASH; Medidata Rave Study Design

description: Human-readable name of the CRF form as displayed in Medidata Rave and study documentation. Examples: 'Adverse Event Form', 'Vital Signs', 'Concomitant Medications'.
Unique Object Identifier (OID) for the CRF form as defined in Medidata Rave and conforming to CDISC ODM standards. Used for cross-system referencing and SDTM mapping. Example: 'AE_FORM_V2'.
reference: CDISC ODM 1.3.2; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

description: Numeric sequence order of this form within its associated visit or study schedule of events. Determines the display order in the EDC and printed CRF booklet.
reference: CDISC ODM 1.3.2; Medidata Rave Study Design

description: Classification of the CRF form by its data collection pattern in Medidata Rave. 'scheduled' forms appear at predefined visits; 'unscheduled' are event-driven; 'common' appear across all visits; 'log' forms capture repeating events (e.g., AE log); 'repeating' forms allow multiple instances per visit.
reference: Medidata Rave Study Design Specification; CDISC CDASH

description: Version identifier of the CRF form definition, following semantic versioning (e.g., '1.0', '2.1', '3.0.1'). Tracks design changes over the trial lifecycle and supports audit trail requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Electronic Source Data

description: Indicates whether this CRF form contains blinded data (e.g., treatment assignment, randomization code) that must be restricted from unblinded personnel during the trial. Supports GCP-compliant blinding controls.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; 21 CFR Part 312

description: Indicates whether this CRF form allows multiple instances per subject per visit (e.g., an Adverse Event log form where each AE is a separate instance). Drives EDC configuration in Medidata Rave.
reference: CDISC ODM 1.3.2; Medidata Rave Study Design Specification

description: Indicates whether Source Data Verification (SDV) is required for data entered on this CRF form. Critical forms (e.g., primary endpoints, safety data) typically require 100% SDV; others may be risk-based.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.3; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; EMA Reflection Paper on Risk-Based Quality Management

description: Indicates whether an electronic signature (e-signature) is required on this CRF form by the investigator or site staff upon completion, as mandated by 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.9; FDA Guidance on Electronic Records

description: Indicates whether this CRF form contributes data to the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population definition. ITT-relevant forms are critical for primary efficacy analysis and regulatory review.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

description: Date and time when this CRF form definition record was last modified. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail, change control, and GCP compliance.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; GDPR Article 5

description: Indicates whether this CRF form captures data for the trial's primary efficacy or safety endpoint (e.g., ORR, PFS, OS). Primary endpoint forms receive heightened monitoring, SDV, and data review scrutiny.
reference: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: The internal Medidata Rave draft version number for this CRF form, distinct from the business version. Tracks incremental design changes within the Rave study build environment prior to promotion to production.
reference: Medidata Rave Study Design Specification; 21 CFR Part 11; CSV Validation

description: The study name as configured in Medidata Rave EDC system, used to identify the parent study context for this CRF form. Supports cross-referencing between the data lakehouse and the source EDC system.
reference: Medidata Rave Study Design Specification; 21 CFR Part 11

business_glossary_term: Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC) Code

description: Code identifying the analytical method or assay used by the laboratory to generate the result (e.g., spectrophotometry, flow cytometry, PCR, ELISA). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBMETHOD. Important for result comparability and method validation documentation.

description: Flag indicating whether the result is within, below, or above the laboratory's normal reference range. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBNRIND. Values: normal, low, high, critically_low, critically_high. Used in safety data listings and shift tables for regulatory submissions.
reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBNRIND); ICH E3; CTCAE v5.0; FDA Data Standards Catalog

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the result value falls outside the laboratory's defined reference range (either below lower limit or above upper limit). reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain; ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the result meets the laboratory's criteria for a panic (critical) value requiring immediate notification to the investigator or site. Supports GCP-compliant safety monitoring and timely SAE/AE reporting obligations.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312.32; CTCAE v5.0; CAP (College of American Pathologists) guidelines

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this laboratory result is associated with a protocol deviation (e.g., specimen collected outside the protocol-defined time window, incorrect specimen type collected). Used for ITT/PP population analysis and regulatory submission deviation summaries.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations

description: Boolean flag indicating whether an open data query (discrepancy) exists for this laboratory result record in Medidata Rave EDC. Used by data managers to track unresolved data issues requiring site clarification before database lock.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Medidata Rave query management

description: Source system record identifier from Medidata Rave EDC for this laboratory result entry. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail back to the originating EDC system.

Upper bound of the laboratory's normal reference range for this test, applicable to the subject's demographic group (age, sex). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTNRHI. Used for normal/abnormal flagging and shift table generation.
reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTNRHI); ICH E3; CTCAE v5.0

description: Lower bound of the laboratory's normal reference range for this test, applicable to the subject's demographic group (age, sex). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTNRLO. Used for normal/abnormal flagging and shift table generation.
reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTNRLO); ICH E3; CTCAE v5.0

description: Date and time when the laboratory result was officially reported and transmitted by the laboratory to the sponsor or EDC system. Used for turnaround time monitoring, GCP compliance (timely reporting of critical values), and data transfer reconciliation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; CAP turnaround time standards

description: Current status of the laboratory result record reflecting its lifecycle in the EDC and central lab workflow. Values: preliminary (initial result), final (verified and released), corrected (amended after initial release), cancelled (result voided), pending (awaiting analysis). Corresponds to HL7 observation status.
reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain; HL7 FHIR Observation.status; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

description: Standardized unit of measure for the laboratory result after conversion to a common unit for cross-site and cross-study comparability. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTRESU. Enables pooled analyses and regulatory submission datasets.
reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTRESU); UCUM; ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBORRES); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

description: Numeric representation of the laboratory result value after standardization and unit conversion. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTRESN. Used for quantitative statistical analyses, shift tables, and outlier detection. Null for non-numeric results.
reference: CDISC SDTM LB domain (LBSTRESN); ICH E3; FDA Data Standards Catalog

Document reference or identifier for the formal monitoring visit report stored in the Trial Master File (TMF) or electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) system.

description: Indicates whether this observation represents the baseline measurement for the subject, used as the reference value for change-from-baseline calculations in efficacy endpoint derivation (e.g., tumor size at baseline for ORR). Corresponds to SDTM ABLFL flag in ADaM datasets.

reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.3; 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

business_glossary_term: Good Clinical Practice (GCP) Training Expiry Date
description: Date on which the current GCP training certification expires. Investigators with expired GCP training must not conduct trial activities. Drives compliance monitoring and site qualification workflows.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.3; FDA GCP Guidance; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

description: Name of the organization or platform that delivered the GCP training (e.g., CITI Program, TransCelerate, sponsor-internal training). Supports audit trail for regulatory inspections.
reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA GCP Guidance; MHRA GCP Inspection findings

description: Name of the hospital, academic medical center, research institution, or private practice with which the investigator is primarily affiliated (e.g., Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, Mayo Clinic). Used for site qualification and regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; FDA Form 1572

description: GCP-defined role of the individual at the investigational site: Principal Investigator (PI) who bears overall responsibility, Sub-Investigator (sub-I) who assists under PI supervision, or Coordinating Investigator who coordinates multi-site activities.

Current lifecycle status of the investigator record. 'Active' indicates the investigator is qualified and currently engaged in trial conduct. 'Disqualified' reflects FDA or regulatory authority debarment or disqualification actions.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.70 (Disqualification of Clinical Investigators); FDA Debarment List

business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Ethics Committee Registration Number
description: Registration number of the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) with which the investigator's site is registered. Required for FDA-regulated trials under 21 CFR Part 56 and ICH E6(R2).
reference: 21 CFR Part 56 (Institutional Review Boards); ICH E6(R2) Section 3; OHRP IRB Registration

description: Indicates whether the investigator is currently listed on the FDA Debarment List or OIG exclusion database. A value of True immediately disqualifies the investigator from participating in any FDA-regulated clinical trial.
reference: 21 CFR Part 312.70; FDCA Section 306; OIG Exclusion Database

description: Legal family name of the principal investigator or sub-investigator as it appears on their medical license and regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; GDPR Article 4

description: Date on which the investigator's medical license expires. Triggers re-qualification workflows to ensure continued GCP-compliant trial conduct. Null if the license has no expiry.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.53; GCP compliance monitoring

description: Name of the regulatory or professional body that issued the medical license (e.g., California Medical Board, General Medical Council UK, Ordre des Médecins France). Required for cross-border trial conduct verification.

State or national medical license number issued by the relevant licensing authority. Required for regulatory submissions and site qualification. Uniquely identifies the investigator's right to practice medicine.
reference: 21 CFR Part 312.53(c); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1.1; State Medical Board regulations

description: Primary board-certified or recognized medical specialty of the investigator (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Cardiology, Neurology). Used to match investigator expertise to trial therapeutic area and protocol requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS); UEMS (European Union of Medical Specialists)

description: Middle name or initial of the investigator as recorded on official credentials. Used for disambiguation when first and last names are not unique.

10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) assigned by CMS to US-based healthcare providers. Used for US-specific investigator identification, cross-referencing with HCP databases, and commercial engagement separation.
reference: HIPAA Administrative Simplification (45 CFR Part 162); CMS NPI Registry; NPPES

description: Persistent digital identifier (ORCID iD) assigned to the investigator by the ORCID registry. Used to uniquely identify researchers across publications, grant applications, and clinical trial registries (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov).
reference: ORCID Standard; ICH E6(R2); ClinicalTrials.gov registration requirements

description: Primary professional phone number for the investigator, used for urgent safety communications, protocol queries, and site monitoring contact. Includes country code for international trials.
reference: ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 4; 21 CFR Part 312

description: Total number of GCP-regulated clinical trials in which the investigator has previously served as PI or sub-investigator. Key feasibility metric used by sponsors and CROs during site selection.
reference: ICH E6(R2); TransCelerate Investigator Registry; FDA Guidance on Site Selection

description: Highest relevant professional or academic degree held by the investigator (e.g., MD, PhD, PharmD). Used in regulatory submissions and delegation logs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MD|DO|PhD|MD-PhD|PharmD|MBBS|MBChB|DVM|Other — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.53

description: Date on which the sponsor or CRO last verified the investigator's qualifications, credentials, and GCP training as part of the site qualification or re-qualification process. Supports audit trail for regulatory inspections.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.6; 21 CFR Part 312.53; FDA Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) readiness

description: Timestamp when the principal investigator master record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and GCP-compliant record management per 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH E6(R2) Section 8; GDPR Article 5

description: Timestamp when the principal investigator master record was most recently modified. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+ data integrity principles

description: Identifier assigned by a national regulatory authority for the investigator's registration to conduct clinical trials (e.g., FDA investigator registration number, EudraCT investigator ID, MHRA registration). Required for IND/NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.
reference: 21 CFR Part 312.53; EudraCT; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation (EU) 536/2014; MHRA

description: Secondary or sub-specialty area of clinical expertise (e.g., Hematologic Oncology, Pediatric Immunology). Provides finer-grained matching for complex or rare disease trials.

Primary therapeutic area(s) in which the investigator has documented clinical trial experience (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neurology). Used for protocol-to-investigator matching and feasibility assessments.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; TransCelerate Investigator Registry; FDA Guidance on Investigator Qualifications

description: Number of years the investigator has been conducting GCP-regulated clinical trials. Used during site feasibility assessments to evaluate investigator experience relative to protocol complexity.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; FDA Guidance on Investigator Qualifications; TransCelerate Site and Investigator Quality Tolerance Limits

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each versioned clinical trial protocol record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for the protocol data product.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 312

Reference to the parent clinical trial to which this protocol version belongs. Links the protocol to the overarching study record in the CTMS.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS

description: Ratio of subjects assigned to each treatment arm (e.g., 1:1, 2:1, 1:1:1). Directly impacts sample size calculations and statistical power. Documented in the randomization section of the protocol.

Sequential integer counter for protocol amendments. Zero (0) indicates the original protocol; each subsequent amendment increments by one. Supports amendment history tracking and regulatory submission traceability.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; FDA Guidance on Protocol Amendments; 21 CFR 312.30

description: Documented justification for protocol changes introduced in this amendment version. Required by regulatory agencies to assess the impact of changes on subject safety, data integrity, and study validity. Null for original protocol (amendment_number = 0).
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; 21 CFR 312.30; EMA Guideline on Protocol Amendments

description: Classification of the amendment's regulatory significance. 'Substantial' amendments require prior regulatory authority approval; 'non_substantial' require notification only; 'administrative' are minor corrections. Determines regulatory submission pathway.
reference: EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014; EMA Guideline on Substantial Modifications; 21 CFR 312.30

description: Date on which the sponsor's internal governance (e.g., Clinical Development Committee) formally approved this protocol version for implementation. Distinct from IRB/IEC approval; triggers eTMF filing in Veeva Vault.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.11; Veeva Vault eTMF; SOPs

description: Level of masking applied to the trial to prevent bias. Double-blind masks both subject and investigator; open-label has no masking. Critical for GCP compliance and regulatory acceptance of efficacy data.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.7; ICH E9(R1); 21 CFR 312

description: National Clinical Trial (NCT) identifier assigned by ClinicalTrials.gov upon trial registration. Mandatory for FDA-regulated trials under FDAAA 801 and required for publication in peer-reviewed journals per ICMJE policy.
reference: FDAAA 801; ICMJE Clinical Trial Registration Policy; WHO ICTRP

description: Timestamp when this protocol record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity standards.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; GDPR Article 5

description: Structural design of the clinical trial. Determines how treatment arms are organized and how subjects are allocated. Informs statistical analysis plan and regulatory review strategy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: parallel|crossover|factorial|single_arm|basket|umbrella|platform — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: ICH E8(R1); ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance

description: Description of the investigational product dose, route of administration, frequency, and duration for each treatment arm (e.g., Drug X 200mg IV Q3W for 12 cycles). Directly linked to CMC and IND/NDA/BLA submissions.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.6; ICH M4E (CTD Module 5); 21 CFR 312.23

description: Date from which this protocol version is operationally effective at investigational sites. For amendments, this is the date sites must implement the changes. Drives site notification and training requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; 21 CFR 312.30; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

description: European Union Drug Regulating Authorities Clinical Trials (EudraCT) registration number assigned by EMA for clinical trials conducted in the EU/EEA. Required for MAA submissions and EU Clinical Trial Regulation compliance.
reference: EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014; EMA EudraCT Database; EMA GCP Guideline

description: Conditions or characteristics that disqualify a subject from enrollment (e.g., prior therapy, comorbidities, contraindications). Complements inclusion criteria to define the eligible study population.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.5; 21 CFR 312.23; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

description: Hypothesis-generating objectives not powering the study, such as biomarker analyses, translational research endpoints, or health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) assessments. Supports future study design and RWE generation.

Boolean flag indicating whether this protocol version has been formally attested as compliant with ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice guidelines. Required for regulatory submissions and audit readiness.
reference: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR 312; EMA GCP Guideline; PIC/S GCP Guide

description: Eligibility criteria that subjects must meet to be enrolled in the trial (e.g., age range, diagnosis, performance status, biomarker positivity). Defines the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) population. Stored as structured free text per protocol.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.5; 21 CFR 312.23; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation

description: FDA-assigned Investigational New Drug (IND) application number under which this protocol is filed. Links the protocol to the regulatory submission record. Required for US clinical trial conduct under 21 CFR Part 312.
reference: 21 CFR 312.23; FDA IND Application; eCTD Module 5

description: Specific disease or medical condition being studied in the trial (e.g., Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer, Rheumatoid Arthritis). Mapped to ICD-10 or MedDRA coding for regulatory submissions.

Date on which the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) granted approval for this protocol version. Milestone date for site activation and GCP compliance documentation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3.1; 21 CFR 56.109; EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014

business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) Approval Reference
description: Reference number or identifier of the IRB/IEC approval for this protocol version. Required for GCP compliance and site activation. Tracked in Veeva Vault eTMF under the Trial Master File structure.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3; 21 CFR 56; EU Clinical Trial Regulation 536/2014

value_regex: Phase I|Phase I/II|Phase II|Phase II/III|Phase III|Phase IV
description: Regulatory development phase of the clinical trial as defined by ICH and FDA guidelines. Determines the study objectives, patient population size, and regulatory pathway (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA).
reference: ICH E8(R1); 21 CFR 312.21; FDA Guidance for Industry

description: Total number of subjects planned for enrollment as determined by the sample size justification in the protocol. Based on statistical power calculations for the primary endpoint. Drives site activation and enrollment planning.
reference: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.5; ICH E6(R2) Section 6.9; FDA Statistical Guidance

description: The principal clinical outcome measure used to evaluate the primary objective (e.g., Overall Survival (OS), Progression-Free Survival (PFS), Objective Response Rate (ORR)). Drives sample size calculation and statistical analysis plan.
reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

description: The principal scientific and clinical objective of the trial as stated in the protocol. Defines the primary endpoint and the key question the study is designed to answer (e.g., demonstrate superiority in Overall Survival).
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.2; ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles

description: Sponsor-assigned unique protocol identifier used across all regulatory submissions, eTMF filings, and CTMS records. Externally known identifier referenced in IND/NDA/BLA/MAA dossiers.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; 21 CFR 312.23; Veeva Vault eTMF

description: Current lifecycle state of this protocol version. 'draft' indicates work-in-progress; 'under_review' indicates IRB/IEC or sponsor review; 'approved' indicates fully authorized for use; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer amendment; 'retired' indicates withdrawn.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Veeva Vault QualityDocs Lifecycle States

description: Method used to randomly allocate subjects to treatment arms. Stratified randomization accounts for prognostic factors; adaptive randomization adjusts allocation ratios based on accumulating data. Documented in the protocol and statistical analysis plan.
reference: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) Section 6.7; FDA Guidance on Randomization

description: Narrative description of the statistical assumptions and power calculations supporting the planned sample size, including assumed effect size, alpha level, power, and dropout rate. Required by ICH E9(R1) and regulatory agencies.
reference: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.5; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials

description: Document identifier or version reference for the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) associated with this protocol version. The SAP details the pre-specified statistical methods for analyzing primary and secondary endpoints per ICH E9(R1).
reference: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) Section 6.9; FDA Statistical Guidance

description: Supporting scientific objectives of the trial beyond the primary endpoint. May include secondary efficacy endpoints (PFS, ORR, QoL), safety objectives, and PK/PD assessments. Stored as free text per protocol document.
Abbreviated or lay-language title of the protocol used in operational communications, CTMS displays, and site-facing materials. Distinct from the full regulatory title.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS

description: Clinical or demographic variables used to stratify randomization to ensure balanced treatment arms (e.g., disease stage, ECOG performance status, geographic region, biomarker status). Stored as free text per protocol specification.
reference: ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Stratified Randomization

description: Broad classification of the study design indicating whether the trial involves an active intervention, passive observation, or special access program. Aligns with ClinicalTrials.gov and EudraCT registration categories.
reference: ICH E8(R1); ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol Registration; EudraCT

description: Disease or medical specialty area targeted by the investigational product (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Used for portfolio planning, regulatory strategy alignment, and commercial analytics.

Full official title of the clinical trial protocol as it appears on the protocol document and regulatory submissions. Typically includes the investigational product name, indication, and study design descriptor.

Timestamp of the most recent modification to this protocol record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity. Enables change detection in the Silver Layer lakehouse pipeline.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5; GDPR Article 5

description: Document identifier in Veeva Vault eTMF where the authoritative protocol document is stored. Enables direct traceability from the data product record to the source document in the electronic Trial Master File.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 8; Veeva Vault eTMF; TMF Reference Model

description: Sequential version identifier for this protocol document (e.g., 1.0, 2.0, 2.1). Each approved amendment increments the version. Used to distinguish original protocol from subsequent amendments.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.1; Veeva Vault eTMF Document Versioning

description: High-level description of the Schedule of Assessments (SoA) including number of study visits, key assessment windows, and follow-up duration. Detailed SoA is maintained in the protocol appendix and Medidata Rave EDC configuration.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6.4; Medidata Rave EDC; CTMS Visit Schedule

Globally unique Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) registry number assigned by the American Chemical Society to uniquely identify the chemical substance. Used for regulatory submissions, procurement, and cross-system compound lookup.
reference: CAS Registry, ICH Q6A, FDA Substance Registration System (SRS)

description: Broad classification of the compound by molecular modality. Drives regulatory pathway selection (NDA vs BLA), manufacturing strategy (chemical synthesis vs biologics), and analytical method requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologic|peptide|adc|oligonucleotide|cell_therapy|rna_therapy|gene_therapy — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH Q6A (small molecules), ICH Q6B (biologics), FDA CDER/CBER classification

description: Internal working name or code name assigned to the compound during discovery (e.g., project code name such as 'ABC-1234'). Used as the primary human-readable label in ELN, LIMS, and CTMS systems before an INN or USAN is assigned.

Current lifecycle status of the compound within the discovery pipeline. 'Active' indicates the compound is under active research; 'promoted' indicates advancement to preclinical or clinical development; 'discontinued' indicates the compound has been deprioritized or terminated.
reference: ICH Q8, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics, 21 CFR Part 312

description: U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) controlled substance schedule classification for the compound (Schedule I–V or not controlled). Determines handling, storage, procurement, and regulatory reporting requirements under the Controlled Substances Act.
reference: DEA Controlled Substances Act (21 USC 812), 21 CFR Part 1308, DEA

description: System-generated timestamp recording when the compound record was first created in the data platform (Silver Layer). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q10, GDPR Article 5(2)

description: Current stage of the compound within the drug discovery pipeline. Tracks progression from target identification through hit identification, hit-to-lead, lead optimization, and candidate selection before IND filing. Used for portfolio reporting and stage-gate decision making.
reference: ICH Q8, ICH M3(R2), FDA IND Guidance 21 CFR Part 312, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Reference identifier linking this compound record to the originating experiment or notebook entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability from the compound master record back to the primary research data and synthesis records.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11, OECD GLP Principles, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

business_glossary_term: New Chemical Entity / New Biological Entity (NCE/NBE) Type
description: Regulatory classification of the compound as a New Chemical Entity (NCE), New Biological Entity (NBE), biosimilar, fixed-dose combination, or prodrug. Determines regulatory exclusivity periods, patent strategy, and submission pathway under FDA, EMA, and ICH guidelines.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108, EMA Guideline on NCE/NBE, ICH Q8

description: Indicates whether the compound and its associated research data have been generated under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) conditions as required for regulatory submissions. GLP compliance is mandatory for safety pharmacology and toxicology studies supporting IND applications.
reference: OECD Principles of GLP, 21 CFR Part 58, EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

description: Globally Harmonized System (GHS) hazard classification for the compound covering health, physical, and environmental hazards (e.g., 'Acute Toxicity Cat. 2, Carcinogen Cat. 1A'). Required for Safety Data Sheet (SDS) preparation, occupational health risk assessment, and EHS compliance.
reference: GHS (UN Purple Book), OSHA HazCom 2012, REACH Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, ICH Q3C

description: Number of hydrogen bond acceptors (HBA) in the compound structure. Key Lipinski Rule of Five parameter (threshold: ≤ 10 HBAs) used in drug-likeness assessment and oral bioavailability prediction during hit-to-lead and lead optimization.
reference: Lipinski Rule of Five, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines

description: Number of hydrogen bond donors (HBD) in the compound structure. Key Lipinski Rule of Five parameter (threshold: ≤ 5 HBDs) used in drug-likeness assessment and oral bioavailability prediction during hit-to-lead and lead optimization.
reference: Lipinski Rule of Five, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines

description: IUPAC International Chemical Identifier (InChI) string providing a standardized, layered representation of the compound's chemical structure. Used for cross-system compound deduplication, registry lookups, and interoperability with external databases (PubChem, ChEMBL). Classified confidential as it encodes proprietary structural IP.
reference: IUPAC InChI Trust, ICH Q6A, FDA SRS

description: Fixed-length 27-character hashed representation of the InChI string (InChIKey). Used as a compact, searchable identifier for compound lookup in external databases (PubChem, ChEMBL, CAS SciFinder) and for deduplication across compound registries.
reference: IUPAC InChI Trust, FDA SRS, PubChem

description: World Health Organization (WHO)-assigned International Nonproprietary Name (INN) for the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Used in regulatory submissions (NDA, BLA, MAA) and scientific communications. May be null for early-stage compounds not yet assigned an INN.
reference: WHO INN Programme, ICH Q6A, 21 CFR Part 314

business_glossary_term: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) Name
description: Systematic chemical name of the compound following International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) nomenclature rules. Provides an unambiguous, internationally recognized chemical identity for regulatory submissions and scientific publications.
reference: IUPAC 2013 Recommendations, ICH Q6A, FDA SRS

description: Date on which the compound record was last reviewed by a qualified scientist or data steward for accuracy, completeness, and continued relevance in the discovery portfolio. Supports data governance and periodic compound library curation activities.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q10, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Designation of the compound library or collection to which this compound belongs within the corporate compound library management system. Drives screening campaign design, compound availability, and resource allocation in HTS and fragment-based drug discovery programs.
reference: ISPE GAMP 5, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics, LIMS - LabWare / SampleManager

description: Logarithm of the octanol-water partition coefficient (LogP), a measure of the compound's lipophilicity. Critical SAR and ADME parameter used to predict membrane permeability, oral bioavailability, and CNS penetration. Lipinski Rule of Five threshold: LogP ≤ 5.
reference: Lipinski Rule of Five, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Described mechanism of action (MOA) of the compound — the biochemical interaction through which the compound produces its pharmacological effect (e.g., 'selective inhibitor of EGFR tyrosine kinase'). Critical for target validation, patent claims, and regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E8, FDA Pharmacology Review Guidance, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Empirical molecular formula of the compound expressed using Hill notation (e.g., C21H30N2O5). Represents the elemental composition and is used in regulatory submissions, analytical method development, and structural verification.
reference: IUPAC Hill System, ICH Q6A, FDA SRS

description: Average molecular weight of the compound expressed in grams per mole (g/mol). Critical physicochemical property used in SAR analysis, ADME profiling, formulation development, and Lipinski Rule of Five drug-likeness assessment.
reference: ICH Q6A, Lipinski Rule of Five, IUPAC

description: Physical state of the compound at standard conditions (solid, liquid, gas, semi-solid). Determines handling procedures, formulation approach, and storage requirements. Captured in the ELN and LIMS at time of compound registration.
reference: ICH Q6A, GMP 21 CFR Part 211, LIMS - LabWare / SampleManager

description: Primary biological molecular target of the compound (e.g., gene name, protein name, receptor, enzyme — such as 'EGFR', 'PD-1', 'BCL-2'). Used in target identification, SAR analysis, and cross-compound target coverage analysis within the discovery portfolio.
reference: ICH E8, ChEMBL Target Nomenclature, UniProt, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Measured chemical purity of the compound expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00%). Determined by analytical methods such as HPLC or NMR. Critical quality attribute (CQA) for assay reliability, GLP compliance, and advancement decisions in hit-to-lead progression.
reference: ICH Q6A, GLP (OECD Principles), 21 CFR Part 58, LIMS - LabWare / SampleManager

description: Date on which the compound was formally registered in the corporate compound registry (IDBS/Dotmatics). Marks the official entry of the compound into the discovery compound library and initiates the compound lifecycle tracking.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11, OECD GLP Principles, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Internally assigned unique registration number for the compound within the corporate compound registry (e.g., IDBS/Dotmatics compound registration system). Serves as the primary business identifier used across discovery, CMC, and regulatory workflows.
reference: ICH Q6A, 21 CFR Part 312, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Number of rotatable bonds in the compound structure. Veber rule parameter (threshold: ≤ 10) used alongside TPSA to predict oral bioavailability and molecular flexibility in SAR and lead optimization analyses.
reference: Veber Rules, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System (SMILES) Notation
description: Canonical SMILES (Simplified Molecular Input Line Entry System) string representing the two-dimensional chemical structure of the compound. Used in cheminformatics, HTS data analysis, SAR modeling, and AI/ML-based drug discovery workflows. Classified confidential as it encodes proprietary structural IP.
reference: Daylight SMILES Specification, ICH Q6A, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Measured or predicted aqueous solubility of the compound expressed in micromolar (µM). Key ADME physicochemical property used in SAR analysis, formulation feasibility assessment, and drug-likeness profiling (Lipinski, Veber rules).
reference: ICH Q6A, Lipinski Rule of Five, ADME Guidelines, LIMS

description: Origin classification of the compound indicating how it was obtained. Synthesized compounds are produced in-house; purchased compounds are acquired from external vendors or CROs; natural products are derived from biological sources. Impacts IP strategy and CMC documentation.
reference: ICH Q11, FDA CMC Guidance, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Recommended storage conditions for the compound (e.g., '-20°C, under nitrogen, protected from light, desiccated'). Ensures compound stability and integrity in the compound library. Derived from stability data and referenced in CoA and compound library management SOPs.
reference: ICH Q1A (Stability Testing), ICH Q6A, GMP 21 CFR Part 211.68, LIMS

description: Primary therapeutic area or disease indication for which the compound is being developed (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience, Cardiovascular). Aligns with the ATC classification system and drives portfolio prioritization and resource allocation decisions.
reference: WHO ATC Classification, ICH E8, FDA Therapeutic Area Guidance

description: Topological Polar Surface Area (TPSA) of the compound expressed in square angstroms (Å²). Used to predict intestinal absorption, blood-brain barrier penetration, and oral bioavailability. Veber rule threshold: TPSA ≤ 140 Å² for oral drugs.
reference: Veber Rules, ICH Q6A, ADME Guidelines, IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: System-generated timestamp recording when the compound record was last modified in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and enables change detection for downstream data consumers and AI/ML pipelines.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q10, GDPR Article 5(2)

description: United States Adopted Name (USAN) assigned by the USAN Council for the compound. Used in US regulatory submissions (NDA/BLA) and US commercial labeling. May differ slightly from INN.

Vendor-assigned catalog or product number for purchased compounds. Used for reorder, procurement traceability, and cross-referencing with vendor CoA and SDS documentation. Applicable only when source_type is 'purchased'.
reference: ICH Q10, SAP S/4HANA MM Module, GMP 21 CFR Part 211

description: Name of the external vendor, CRO, or supplier from whom the compound was purchased or sourced, if applicable. Relevant for purchased compounds and natural product extracts. Used for procurement traceability, vendor qualification, and supply chain management.
reference: ICH Q10, GMP 21 CFR Part 211, SAP S/4HANA MM Module

Foreign key linking to the vendor supplying this compound

Vendor-specific catalog number or SKU for this compound in the vendor's product catalog. Used for purchase order line item specification.
Indicates whether a Certificate of Analysis (CoA) must be provided by the vendor with each shipment of this compound. CoA requirements vary by compound criticality and vendor qualification status.
Date of the most recent purchase order placed for this compound from this vendor. Used to track active supply relationships and vendor performance history.

business_glossary_term: Minimum Order Quantity Unit of Measure
description: Unit of measure for the minimum order quantity (gram, milligram, kilogram, vial, unit)

Indicates whether this vendor is designated as the preferred supplier for this specific compound based on quality, price, reliability, and strategic relationship. A compound may have multiple approved vendors but only one preferred vendor.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the unit price (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP)
Contractually agreed minimum purity specification for this compound from this vendor (e.g., ≥95%, ≥98%, ≥99.5%). Purity requirements may vary by vendor capability and intended use.
Number of quality issues (out-of-specification results, failed CoA, contamination) reported for this compound from this vendor. Used for vendor performance tracking and sourcing decisions.
Negotiated price per unit (gram, milligram, or vial) for this compound from this vendor. Price varies by vendor based on volume commitments, purity specifications, and contract terms.

Unique surrogate identifier for each compound synthesis record in the discovery domain. Primary key for the compound_synthesis data product. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — a discrete synthesis event with its own lifecycle, reagents, conditions, and outcomes.
reference: ICH Q11 (Development and Manufacture of Drug Substances)

description: Reference to the compound entity that was synthesized in this experiment. Links the synthesis record to the master compound registry (NCE/NBE catalogue).
reference: ICH Q11; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics compound registry

description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Synthesis activities consume reagents, labor, and equipment charged to cost centers for project costing, resource planning, and financial reporting. Essential for medicinal chemistry budget management

Foreign key linking to regulatory.dmf. Business justification: Synthesis routes and manufacturing processes are documented in Drug Master Files (Type II DMF for API). Real business process: CMC teams reference synthesis data when preparing or updating DMFs for re

Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Individual synthesis activities are charged to internal orders for cost-per-compound tracking, essential for portfolio economics, make-vs-buy decisions, and CRO cost benchmarking in pharmaceutical dis

Foreign key linking to intellectual.invention_disclosure. Business justification: Novel synthetic routes and processes are disclosed as inventions; disclosure linkage tracks process IP, supports patent filing for manufacturing methods, and protects CMC innovations.

Foreign key linking to discovery.lead_series. Business justification: Compound synthesis efforts by medicinal chemistry teams are organized by lead series. Each synthesis produces an analog within a specific chemical series. The synthesis table currently has series_code

Reference to the biological target (protein, enzyme, receptor, or pathway) against which this compound was synthesized. Links synthesis provenance to target identification and MOA studies in the discovery domain.
reference: ChEMBL target classification; UniProt; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Reference to the medicinal chemist who performed the synthesis. Supports attribution, GLP accountability, and ELN audit trail requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); ICH Q10

description: Reference to the drug discovery project under which this synthesis was conducted. Enables project-level portfolio reporting, resource tracking, and compound series management.
reference: ICH Q10; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics project management

description: Reference to the defined synthetic route used for this synthesis event. A route captures the ordered sequence of chemical transformations from starting materials to target compound.
reference: ICH Q11; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics route registry

description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Custom synthesis frequently outsourced to CRO/CMO vendors. Procurement manages vendor qualification, quality agreements, IP protection clauses, and service delivery for outsourced synthesis operations

Timestamp when the synthesis record received formal electronic approval in the ELN by the supervising scientist. Distinct from record creation; captures the GLP-required second-person review event for data integrity.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); OECD Series on Principles of GLP

description: Alphanumeric batch identifier assigned to the synthesized compound lot. Used for inventory tracking, biological testing assignment, and downstream traceability through the discovery pipeline. Aligns with SAP MM batch management.
reference: 21 CFR Part 211.68; ICH Q7; SAP S/4HANA MM module

description: Name and loading of the catalyst or catalytic system used in the reaction (e.g., Pd(PPh3)4, Pd2(dba)3/XPhos, DMAP). Null if the reaction is uncatalysed. Critical for SAR and process chemistry knowledge management.

Classification of the synthesized compound by modality. Distinguishes New Chemical Entities (NCE), New Biological Entities (NBE), peptides, oligonucleotides, PROTACs, fragments, and natural product derivatives. Drives downstream development pathway and regulatory strategy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NCE|NBE|peptide|oligonucleotide|PROTAC|fragment|natural_product_derivative — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH M9; FDA CDER Drug Classification; EMA Guideline on the Investigation of Bioequivalence

description: Timestamp when this synthesis record was first created in the system (ELN or data lakehouse). Mandatory audit field for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance and GLP data integrity requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

description: Unique experiment identifier from the Electronic Lab Notebook system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics) that documents the full experimental procedure, observations, and raw data for this synthesis. Provides traceability back to the authoritative source record.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Free-text description of the reason for synthesis failure or cancellation when synthesis_status is 'failed' or 'cancelled'. Captures root cause information (e.g., no reaction observed, product decomposition, purification failure, starting material unavailable) to support process learning and SAR knowledge management.
reference: ICH Q10 (Pharmaceutical Quality System); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Indicates whether this synthesis was conducted in full compliance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations. GLP-compliant syntheses are required for compounds entering formal preclinical safety studies. True = GLP compliant; False = non-GLP (exploratory research).
reference: OECD Principles of GLP; 21 CFR Part 58; OECD Series on Principles of GLP and Compliance Monitoring

description: GHS/CLP hazard classification of the synthesized compound based on its physicochemical and toxicological properties. Governs safe handling, storage, and disposal procedures in the laboratory. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: non_hazardous|flammable|toxic|corrosive|oxidising|highly_toxic|environmental_hazard — promote to reference product]
reference: GHS (Globally Harmonised System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals); EU CLP Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008; OSHA HazCom 2012

description: Purity of the synthesized compound as determined by High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC), expressed as area percentage. A Critical Quality Attribute (CQA) for compound registration and screening eligibility. Compounds typically require ≥95% purity for HTS submission.
reference: ICH Q6A (Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria); GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); USP <621>

description: Empirical molecular formula of the synthesized compound (e.g., C18H21N3O2). Derived from structural confirmation data. Used for compound identity verification, registry matching, and regulatory documentation.
reference: IUPAC nomenclature; ICH Q6A; Dotmatics / IDBS compound registry

description: Calculated molecular weight of the synthesized compound in grams per mole (g/mol), derived from the confirmed chemical structure. Used for stoichiometric calculations, Lipinski rule-of-five assessment, and compound library profiling.
reference: ICH Q6A; IUPAC; Dotmatics / IDBS compound registry

description: Purity of the synthesized compound as determined by quantitative Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, expressed as percentage. Orthogonal purity assessment to HPLC; used for structural confirmation and identity verification per GLP requirements.
reference: ICH Q6A; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); USP <761>

description: Actual mass of isolated compound product in milligrams. Used to determine availability for biological screening, ADME assays, and compound library registration. Directly linked to synthesis scale and yield.
reference: ICH Q11; LIMS (LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager)

description: Method used to purify the crude reaction product to achieve the required purity specification (e.g., column chromatography, preparative HPLC, recrystallisation, trituration). Influences final yield and purity outcomes and informs process development decisions.
reference: ICH Q11; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Total elapsed time of the synthesis reaction in hours. A Critical Process Parameter (CPP) used in reaction optimization and SAR/process correlation studies.
reference: ICH Q8; ICH Q11; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP)

description: Temperature at which the synthesis reaction was conducted, expressed in degrees Celsius. A Critical Process Parameter (CPP) that directly influences reaction selectivity, yield, and purity. Captured from ELN experimental conditions.
reference: ICH Q8 (Pharmaceutical Development); ICH Q11; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP)

description: Free-text or structured description of the key reagents and their stoichiometric equivalents used in the synthesis (e.g., 'K2CO3 (2.0 eq), Pd(OAc)2 (5 mol%), SPhos (10 mol%)'). Supports reproducibility and GLP documentation requirements.
reference: GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q11

description: Indicates whether the synthesized compound has been registered in the corporate compound library for HTS and biological screening. True = registered and available for screening; False = not yet registered or failed registration criteria (e.g., purity < 95%).
reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics compound registry; LIMS (LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager)

description: Canonical SMILES (Simplified Molecular-Input Line-Entry System) string representing the two-dimensional chemical structure of the synthesized compound. Machine-readable format used for cheminformatics, SAR analysis, and compound database registration in Dotmatics.
reference: Daylight Chemical Information Systems SMILES specification; ICH Q6A; Dotmatics / IDBS

description: Name of the primary solvent or solvent system used in the synthesis reaction (e.g., DMF, THF, DCM, EtOH, water). Influences reaction kinetics, selectivity, and downstream purification strategy. Relevant to ICH Q3C solvent classification for later-stage development.
reference: ICH Q3C (Residual Solvents); ICH Q11; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP)

description: Required storage condition for the synthesized compound to maintain stability and integrity (e.g., room temperature, 2–8°C, −20°C, −80°C, nitrogen atmosphere, desiccator). Derived from compound physicochemical properties and stability data.
reference: ICH Q1A (Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products); LIMS (LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager)

description: Physical storage location of the synthesized compound batch (e.g., freezer ID, rack, position in compound management system). Enables inventory management and sample retrieval for biological testing.
reference: LIMS (LabWare / Thermo Fisher SampleManager); GDP (Good Distribution Practice); ICH Q1A (Stability Testing)

description: Analytical technique(s) used to confirm the chemical structure of the synthesized compound (e.g., 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, LCMS, HRMS, IR, X-ray crystallography). Structural confirmation is mandatory for compound registration and GLP compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 1H-NMR|13C-NMR|LCMS|HRMS|IR|X-ray|multiple — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: ICH Q6A; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); 21 CFR Part 58

description: Calendar date on which the synthesis reaction was initiated. Principal business event date for this transaction record. Used for timeline tracking, GLP compliance dating, and SAR trend analysis.
reference: GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q11

description: Human-readable, externally-known business identifier for this synthesis event, typically assigned by the ELN (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Follows site-specific numbering conventions (e.g., MED-SYN-000123). Used for cross-referencing in lab notebooks, SAR databases, and regulatory submissions.
reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; 21 CFR Part 11; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP)

description: Scientific purpose for which this compound was synthesized. Classifies the synthesis within the drug discovery workflow (e.g., hit confirmation from HTS, lead optimisation, SAR exploration, ADME probe, tool compound, library synthesis). Enables portfolio analytics and resource allocation reporting.
reference: ICH Q8; FDA Guidance for Industry: Drug Interaction Studies; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Molar scale of the synthesis reaction expressed in millimoles (mmol). Determines reagent quantities, expected yield mass, and suitability for downstream biological screening (e.g., HTS vs. focused assay).
reference: ICH Q11; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP)

description: Current lifecycle state of the synthesis experiment. Tracks progression from planned through execution to completion or failure. Drives workflow routing in the medicinal chemistry pipeline.
reference: ICH Q10 (Pharmaceutical Quality System); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Name or classification of the synthetic methodology applied (e.g., Suzuki coupling, reductive amination, Buchwald-Hartwig amination, solid-phase synthesis). Enables SAR analysis by correlating method with yield and purity outcomes.
reference: ICH Q11; IUPAC nomenclature; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this synthesis record. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail compliance and data integrity monitoring in GLP environments.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); ICH Q10

description: Isolated yield of the target compound expressed as a percentage of the theoretical maximum based on the limiting reagent. A primary quantitative outcome metric for synthesis efficiency and SAR optimization. Range: 0.00–100.00.
reference: ICH Q11; GLP (OECD Principles of GLP); IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics

reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics compound registry; ICH Q8

reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics HTS module; ICH Q8

reference: FDA NCE/NBE Classification; ICH M4; 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA) / Part 601 (BLA)

reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics assay results; ICH M4 Pharmacology; ChEMBL bioactivity standards
