business_glossary_term: Absorption Distribution Metabolism Excretion (ADME) Profile ID
description: Unique surrogate identifier for each ADME profiling record in the discovery domain. Primary key for the adme_profile data product. Entity role: TRANSACTION_HEADER — captures a discrete ADME assay event with its own lifecycle and results.
reference: ICH M10 Bioanalytical Method Validation; 21 CFR Part 312

description: Reference to the standardized ADME assay panel applied during this profiling run, defining the battery of tests performed (e.g., Tier 1 ADME screen, full ADME panel).
reference: LabWare LIMS; ICH M10; GLP 21 CFR Part 58

description: Reference to the compound under ADME evaluation, linking to the compound master record in the discovery compound library. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE category (compound is the principal resource being profiled).
Reference to the ADME scientist responsible for executing and reviewing this profiling run. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER PARTY_REFERENCE category for the responsible scientist.
Reference to the drug discovery project under which this ADME profiling was conducted, enabling project-level aggregation of ADME data for compound progression decisions.

Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: ADME data is required in Module 4.2.2 (pharmacokinetics) of regulatory submissions. Real regulatory requirement: nonclinical PK/ADME studies must be submitted with traceable study reports. Critical fo

Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: ADME profiling frequently outsourced to specialized CRO vendors for permeability, metabolism, protein binding, and PK studies. Vendor qualification, quality agreements, GLP compliance, and data qualit

Composite numerical risk score (e.g., 0–100) summarizing overall ADME liability across solubility, permeability, metabolic stability, and DDI risk dimensions. Used for compound ranking and portfolio prioritization in discovery.
reference: ICH Q6A; internal compound scoring framework; FDA IND Guidance

description: Concentration of the compound used in the ADME assay incubation, expressed in micromolar (µM). Required for result interpretation and inter-assay comparability; standard concentrations are typically 1–10 µM.
reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; LabWare LIMS; ICH M10

description: Calendar date on which the ADME assay panel was executed in the laboratory. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category (day-level precision for assay scheduling and trending).

Unbound brain-to-plasma concentration ratio (Kp,uu,brain), the quantitative measure of CNS penetration accounting for plasma protein binding. Values >0.3 indicate meaningful CNS exposure; used in CNS drug discovery programs.
reference: FDA CNS Drug Development Guidance; EMA Guideline on Pharmacokinetics

description: Indicates whether the compound demonstrates blood-brain barrier penetration based on in vitro BBB assay (e.g., MDCK-MDR1, hCMEC/D3) or in vivo brain-to-plasma ratio. Critical for CNS-targeted and CNS-safety assessments.
reference: FDA CNS Drug Development Guidance; EMA Guideline on Pharmacokinetics; ICH S7A

description: Estimated oral bioavailability percentage (%F) derived from permeability, solubility, and metabolic stability data using predictive ADME models. Key compound progression criterion for oral drug candidates.
reference: FDA BCS Guidance; ICH M9; EMA BCS-based Biowaiver Guideline

description: Predicted in vivo hepatic clearance in mL/min/kg, scaled from in vitro microsomal intrinsic clearance using the well-stirred liver model. Used to estimate dose and dosing interval in early drug discovery.
reference: ICH M10; FDA Pharmacokinetics Guidance; EMA Guideline on Pharmacokinetics

description: Timestamp when this ADME profile record was first created in the system. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category. Supports 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records audit trail.
Half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) for CYP2C9 enzyme inhibition in µM. CYP2C9 metabolizes warfarin and NSAIDs; inhibition is a critical DDI safety signal for regulatory submissions.
reference: FDA Drug Interaction Guidance (2020); EMA Guideline on Investigation of Drug Interactions; ICH M12

description: Half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) for CYP2D6 enzyme inhibition in µM. CYP2D6 metabolizes ~25% of marketed drugs; inhibition is a major DDI liability assessed by FDA and EMA.
reference: FDA Drug Interaction Guidance (2020); EMA Guideline on Investigation of Drug Interactions; ICH M12

description: Half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) for CYP3A4 enzyme inhibition in µM. CYP3A4 metabolizes ~50% of marketed drugs; inhibition predicts drug-drug interaction (DDI) liability. Key regulatory safety flag.
reference: FDA Drug Interaction Guidance (2020); EMA Guideline on Investigation of Drug Interactions; ICH M12

description: Composite boolean flag indicating whether the compound exhibits significant CYP inhibition risk (any CYP isoform IC50 below the regulatory concern threshold, typically <10 µM). Used for rapid compound triage and progression gating.
reference: FDA Drug Interaction Guidance (2020); EMA Guideline on Investigation of Drug Interactions; ICH M12

description: Ratio of basolateral-to-apical (B→A) over apical-to-basolateral (A→B) permeability in Caco-2 assay. Values >2 indicate active efflux transport (e.g., P-gp substrate), impacting oral bioavailability and CNS penetration.
reference: FDA BCS Guidance; ICH M9; EMA Guideline on Investigation of Drug Interactions

description: Reference identifier linking this ADME profile to the corresponding experiment entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics), providing traceability to raw experimental data and GLP documentation.
reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; 21 CFR Part 11; IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN

description: Predicted or measured plasma half-life of the compound in hours, derived from in vitro microsomal clearance data using allometric scaling or measured directly in in vivo PK studies. Informs dosing frequency predictions.
reference: ICH M10; FDA Pharmacokinetics Guidance; EMA Guideline on Pharmacokinetics

description: Intrinsic metabolic clearance measured in human liver microsomes (HLM), expressed as µL/min/mg protein. Used to predict in vivo hepatic clearance and half-life via well-stirred liver model. Critical for dose prediction.
reference: ICH M10; FDA Drug Metabolism Guidance; EMA Guideline on Drug Interactions

business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Sample ID
description: Sample identifier assigned by the LIMS (LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager) for the compound sample used in this ADME assay. Enables traceability from ADME result back to physical sample chain of custody.
reference: GLP 21 CFR Part 58; LabWare LIMS; Thermo Fisher SampleManager

description: Free-text field for ADME scientist observations, anomalies, assay deviations, or contextual notes relevant to interpreting the ADME profile results. Supports GLP documentation requirements.

business_glossary_term: Parallel Artificial Membrane Permeability Assay (PAMPA) Permeability (nm/s)

reference: FDA Drug Interaction Guidance; EMA Guideline on Investigation of Drug Interactions; ICH M12

description: Percentage of compound bound to plasma proteins (albumin, alpha-1-acid glycoprotein) measured by equilibrium dialysis or ultrafiltration. Determines free fraction available for pharmacological activity and clearance.

description: Analytical method used to determine plasma protein binding percentage. Rapid equilibrium dialysis (RED) is the industry standard; method choice affects result interpretation and cross-study comparability.
reference: ICH M10; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this ADME profiling run, used in ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics) and LIMS cross-referencing. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this ADME profile record. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category. Supports 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements.

description: Narrative summary of the compound's Mechanism of Action (MOA) — how it interacts with the molecular target to produce the desired pharmacological effect. Sourced from ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics) and used in IND applications and regulatory submissions.

The drug modality class of the nominated development candidate, distinguishing New Chemical Entities (NCE) from New Biological Entities (NBE) and advanced therapy types. Determines regulatory pathway (NDA vs BLA) and CMC strategy.
reference: FDA CDER/CBER Classification; ICH M4Q; 21 CFR Parts 210/211/312

reference: ICH M4S; SAR Analysis SOP; EMA Guideline on Non-Clinical Safety Studies

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this candidate nomination record originated or was primarily authored (e.g., IDBS E-WorkBook, Dotmatics, LIMS). Supports data lineage and Silver layer provenance tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ISPE GAMP 5; Internal Data Governance Policy

description: Description of the intended patient population for the proposed indication, including relevant biomarker stratification, disease stage, or demographic characteristics (e.g., adult patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC, pediatric patients with SMA). Informs clinical trial design.

Primary reason why the patient discontinued treatment with this compound. Critical for safety analysis, efficacy assessment, and regulatory reporting.

Overall clinical response of the patient to the compound treatment, typically using standardized response criteria (e.g., RECIST for oncology). Captures efficacy outcome for this exposure.
Clinical trial treatment arm to which the patient was randomized or assigned (active, placebo, comparator, combination). Determines which compound or regimen the patient received.
Total duration of compound exposure expressed in days. Used for exposure-response analysis, safety signal detection, and pharmacovigilance reporting.
Actual date of last dose administration of the compound to the patient. Used for exposure duration calculation and follow-up period determination.
Actual date of first dose administration of the compound to the patient. Used for exposure window calculation and temporal safety analysis.

description: Specific batch or lot identifier of the compound used in this study. Critical for reproducibility, traceability, and investigation of batch-to-batch variability in results.

description: Highest concentration of the compound tested in this study, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Defines the upper bound of the concentration-response range; used to assess ceiling effects and cytotoxicity thresholds.
reference: ICH S7A; ICH M10; OECD Test Guidelines; LabWare LIMS

description: Lowest concentration of the compound tested in this study, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Defines the lower bound of the concentration-response range used for dose-response modelling.
reference: ICH S7A; ICH M10; OECD Test Guidelines; LabWare LIMS

description: Number of distinct concentration levels tested in the dose-response series. Indicates the resolution of the concentration-response curve and the robustness of derived potency estimates.
reference: ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines; LabWare LIMS

description: Indicates whether cytotoxic effects were observed at the tested concentration range. A True value signals that the primary endpoint result may be confounded by non-specific cell death and requires scientific interpretation caution.

description: Indicates whether this study confirmed the hypothesised mechanism of action (MOA) for the compound at the tested target. A True value supports progression to the next stage of hit-to-lead development.

description: Unit of measurement for the primary result value (e.g., nM, µM, %, fold-change). Required for correct scientific interpretation and cross-study comparability.

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: GLP compliance mandates study director accountability with traceable qualifications. FDA inspections verify study director training, experience, and authority. FK to employee enables verification of G
Total number of animals used across all dose groups in the study. Required for IACUC protocol compliance, 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) reporting, and statistical power justification.
reference: PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; IACUC regulations; 21 CFR Part 58.90

description: Sex of the animals used in the study (male, female, or both sexes). Relevant for sex-specific PK/PD differences, hormonal effects, and regulatory requirements for balanced study design.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58.90; ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines

description: Species of animal used in the in vivo study (e.g., mouse, rat, dog, non-human primate). Determines applicable regulatory guidelines, PK/PD scaling factors, and IACUC protocol requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mouse|rat|rabbit|dog|monkey|minipig|hamster|guinea_pig — promote to reference product]
reference: 21 CFR Part 58; ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines; IACUC regulations (PHS Policy)

description: Specific strain or substrain of the animal species used (e.g., C57BL/6 mouse, Sprague-Dawley rat, Beagle dog). Strain selection impacts pharmacological response, metabolic profile, and cross-study comparability.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58.90; OECD GLP Principles; ICH S7A

description: Date on which the in vivo study was completed (last animal procedure, sample collection, or terminal endpoint). Null if the study is still in progress or was terminated early. Used for study report timelines and regulatory submission planning.

Specific batch or lot number of the test article (compound) used in this study, as recorded in the LIMS or compound management system. Critical for traceability, reproducibility, and GLP compliance — links to Certificate of Analysis (CoA) for purity and characterization data.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58.105; OECD GLP Principles Section 8; ICH Q6A

description: Internal compound registration number or code (e.g., NCE/NBE identifier from the compound library) as assigned in the ELN or compound management system. Denormalized here for operational traceability without requiring a join. Classified confidential due to IP sensitivity.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58; ICH Q6A; GDPR Article 25 (data minimisation)

description: Name of the facility (internal research site or external CRO/CMO) where the in vivo study was physically conducted. Relevant for multi-site studies, CRO oversight, and GLP facility qualification tracking.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58.3; OECD GLP Principles; PIC/S GLP

description: Timestamp when this in vivo study record was first created in the system (ISO 8601 format with timezone offset). Audit trail field required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance and data lineage tracking in the lakehouse silver layer.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; OECD GLP Principles; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

description: Indicates whether the study was outsourced to a Contract Research Organization (CRO) rather than conducted in-house. Drives CRO oversight workflows, contract management linkage, and sponsor responsibility documentation under GLP.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58.10; OECD GLP Principles; ICH M3(R2)

description: Frequency of compound administration during the study (e.g., single dose, once daily, twice daily). Defines the dosing regimen and is critical for PK/PD modeling and exposure calculations.
reference: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58

description: Comma-separated list of dose levels tested in the study (e.g., '1, 3, 10, 30' in the unit specified by dose_unit). Captures the full dose range including vehicle/control group. Stored as a structured string for multi-dose studies; individual dose group records are managed in the study design detail.
reference: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58

description: Route of compound administration to the animals (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous). Directly impacts bioavailability, PK profile, and translational relevance to the intended clinical route. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intraperitoneal|intramuscular|inhalation|topical|intranasal — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines; 21 CFR Part 58

description: Unit of measurement for dose levels administered in the study (e.g., mg/kg, µg/kg). Standardized unit required for cross-study comparability, allometric scaling, and regulatory submission.
reference: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; OECD Test Guidelines

description: Description of the primary efficacy endpoint measured in the study (e.g., tumor volume reduction, blood glucose normalization, survival rate, biomarker inhibition percentage). Defines the scientific success criterion for the study and links to the compound's mechanism of action (MOA).
reference: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; FDA Guidance: Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials

description: Narrative summary of the primary efficacy outcome observed in the study (e.g., '60% tumor growth inhibition at 10 mg/kg QD', 'statistically significant reduction in target biomarker at all dose levels'). Supports portfolio review and go/no-go decision-making.
reference: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58.185

description: Reference identifier linking this study record to the corresponding experiment or notebook entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability to raw experimental data, protocols, and observations recorded at the bench.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles

description: Indicates whether the study was conducted in full compliance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations (21 CFR Part 58 / OECD GLP Principles). GLP-compliant studies are required for regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA). Non-GLP studies are exploratory/screening studies.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ICH M3(R2); EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

description: Date on which the IACUC protocol was formally approved, authorizing the commencement of animal studies. Study start_date must not precede this date. Critical for GLP compliance and regulatory audit readiness.
reference: PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; Animal Welfare Act (9 CFR); 21 CFR Part 58

business_glossary_term: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) Protocol Number
description: Unique protocol number assigned by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) approving the animal use in this study. Mandatory for all in vivo studies conducted in the US under the Animal Welfare Act and PHS Policy. Required for regulatory submissions and audit.
reference: PHS Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals; Animal Welfare Act (9 CFR); 21 CFR Part 58

business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Study Reference
description: Reference identifier linking this study record to the corresponding study or sample set in the LIMS (LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager). Enables traceability of sample management, analytical results, and chain of custody for study samples.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ISO/IEC 17025

description: No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) determined from the study, expressed in mg/kg. The highest dose at which no statistically or biologically significant adverse effects were observed. Critical for safety margin calculations, human dose prediction, and IND-enabling study packages.
reference: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; FDA Guidance: Estimating the Maximum Safe Starting Dose; 21 CFR Part 58

business_glossary_term: Pharmacokinetics (PK) Area Under the Curve AUC (ng·mL⁻¹·h)
description: Area Under the plasma concentration-time Curve (AUC) representing total systemic exposure to the compound, expressed in ng·mL⁻¹·h. Fundamental PK parameter for bioavailability assessment, dose proportionality analysis, and PK/PD modeling.
reference: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Bioavailability and Bioequivalence Studies; ICH S7A

description: Absolute oral bioavailability (%F) of the compound expressed as a percentage, calculated as the ratio of AUC after oral administration to AUC after intravenous administration. Critical for oral drug candidate selection and dose prediction.
reference: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Bioavailability and Bioequivalence Studies

description: Systemic clearance (CL) of the compound normalized to body weight (mL/min/kg). Represents the volume of plasma cleared of the compound per unit time. Key parameter for predicting human PK and first-in-human dose selection.
reference: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Pharmacokinetics; ICH S7A

description: Maximum observed plasma concentration (Cmax) of the compound following administration, expressed in nanograms per milliliter (ng/mL). Key PK parameter for exposure assessment, dose-response modeling, and allometric scaling to human dose prediction.
reference: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Pharmacokinetics in Patients with Impaired Renal Function; ICH S7A

description: Terminal elimination half-life (t½) of the compound in hours, representing the time required for plasma concentration to decrease by 50%. Used for dosing frequency determination, accumulation prediction, and species-to-human PK translation.
reference: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Pharmacokinetics; ICH S7A

description: Apparent volume of distribution (Vd) of the compound normalized to body weight (L/kg). Indicates the extent of tissue distribution versus plasma binding. Critical for PK/PD modeling and human dose prediction via allometric scaling.
reference: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance: Pharmacokinetics; ICH S7A

description: Full name of the Principal Investigator (PI) responsible for the scientific design and execution of the study. May differ from the Study Director in multi-site or CRO-conducted studies. Classified confidential as an internal personnel reference.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP (for reference alignment)

description: Date on which the in vivo study was initiated (first animal dosing or first experimental procedure). The principal real-world event date for this study record. Used for timeline tracking, regulatory reporting, and study portfolio management.

Total planned duration of the in vivo study in calendar days from first dose to last observation/sample collection. Used for study planning, resource allocation, and regulatory classification (e.g., single-dose vs. repeat-dose toxicology).
reference: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique study identifier assigned by the research organization or LIMS (e.g., IDBS/Dotmatics ELN). Used for cross-referencing in regulatory submissions, study reports, and IACUC protocols. Follows the site-specific numbering convention.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58.185; OECD GLP Principles; ICH S7A/S7B

description: Drug discovery pipeline phase during which this in vivo study was conducted. Indicates the maturity of the compound under investigation and the decision gate this study supports (e.g., hit-to-lead progression, candidate selection).
reference: ICH M3(R2); FDA Guidance for Industry: Drug Interaction Studies

description: Unique identifier of the final GLP or non-GLP study report generated upon study completion. Used for cross-referencing in regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, eCTD), dossier compilation, and audit trail. Null until the study report is issued.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58.185; OECD GLP Principles Section 9; ICH M4S (eCTD Module 4)

description: Current lifecycle state of the in vivo study. Drives workflow routing, data lock decisions, and reporting eligibility. 'Terminated' indicates early discontinuation with a documented reason; 'cancelled' indicates the study was never initiated.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ICH M3(R2)

description: Descriptive title of the in vivo study as recorded in the electronic lab notebook (ELN) or LIMS. Provides a human-readable summary of the study objective, compound, and species (e.g., 'Single-dose PK study of Compound XYZ-001 in Sprague-Dawley rats').

Classification of the primary scientific objective of the in vivo study. Drives downstream data capture requirements and regulatory reporting pathways. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: efficacy|pharmacokinetics|pharmacodynamics|tolerability|safety|pk_pd|dose_range_finding|moa — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH S7A; ICH S7B; ICH M3(R2); 21 CFR Part 58

description: Date on which the study was prematurely terminated, if applicable. Distinct from completion_date (planned end). Populated only when study_status is 'terminated'. Requires a corresponding termination_reason.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58; OECD GLP Principles; ICH M3(R2)

description: Documented reason for early termination of the study (e.g., unexpected toxicity, compound supply failure, scientific decision to deprioritize). Required when termination_date is populated. Supports portfolio decision audit trail.

Summary of tolerability observations recorded during the study, including body weight changes, clinical signs, and any adverse findings at tested dose levels. Informs the therapeutic index assessment and maximum tolerated dose (MTD) determination for candidate progression.
reference: ICH M3(R2); ICH S7A; 21 CFR Part 58; OECD Test Guidelines

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this in vivo study record (ISO 8601 format with timezone offset). Required for change tracking, audit compliance under 21 CFR Part 11, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks lakehouse.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; OECD GLP Principles; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the assay master record in the discovery domain. Primary key for the assay data product. Role classification: MASTER_RESOURCE.
reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN internal object model

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.gxp_obligation. Business justification: Assays used for regulatory submissions must comply with specific GxP obligations (GLP validation, data integrity, method validation). Obligation mapping drives validation requirements, inspection prep

Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: Assays are designed to screen against specific molecular targets. The assay table currently has target_name and target_class as denormalized STRING attributes. Adding molecular_target_id FK allows joi

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: GxP compliance and regulatory inspections require traceable accountability for assay validation and execution. Responsible scientist must link to qualified employee record for training verification, e

Externally-known, human-readable unique code assigned to the assay within the ELN or LIMS (e.g., ASY-HTS0042). Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used for cross-system referencing between IDBS/Dotmatics, LabWare LIMS, and SAP QM.
reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; LabWare LIMS; ICH Q2(R1)

description: Full descriptive name of the assay as registered in the ELN (e.g., 'EGFR Kinase Inhibition HTRF Assay'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used in scientific reports, regulatory submissions, and compound screening dashboards.
reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; ICH M10 (Bioanalytical Method Validation)

description: Primary scientific classification of the assay based on its biological or chemical mode of measurement. Serves as the CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Drives downstream SAR analysis workflows and compound triage decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: biochemical|cell_based|phenotypic|ADME|toxicity|binding|functional — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH S7A/S7B (Safety Pharmacology); FDA Guidance on Drug Interaction Studies; IDBS Dotmatics assay taxonomy

description: Indicates whether the assay has been adapted and validated for automated liquid handling platforms (e.g., Hamilton, Tecan, Beckman Coulter). Determines eligibility for inclusion in HTS screening campaigns and impacts throughput capacity planning.
reference: ISPE GAMP 5; ANSI/SLAS Microplate Standards; IDBS E-WorkBook automation integration

description: Name of the cell line used in cell-based assays (e.g., HEK293, HeLa, Jurkat, A549, MCF-7). Null for biochemical or cell-free assays. Required for assay reproducibility and cross-site comparability. Cell line authentication records are maintained in the ELN.
reference: ATCC cell line standards; ISPE GAMP 5; ICH Q5D (Cell Substrates); LabWare LIMS biological material registry

description: Percentage coefficient of variation (%CV) of the assay signal across replicate measurements, representing assay precision and reproducibility. Typically required to be ≤ 15% for HTS assays and ≤ 20% for bioanalytical assays per ICH Q2(R1). Stored from the assay validation run.
reference: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

description: Unit of measurement for compound concentrations used in the assay (e.g., nM, µM, mM). Standardizes concentration reporting across compound screening results and SAR analysis. Required for dose-response curve fitting and IC50/EC50 calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: nM|uM|mM|mg_mL|ug_mL|ng_mL|pM — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: ICH Q2(R1); IUPAC nomenclature; LabWare LIMS unit registry

description: Estimated reagent and consumable cost per assay well in US dollars. Used for screening campaign cost modeling, budget planning, and make-vs-buy decisions for outsourcing to CROs. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA MM procurement data and lab supply records.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO (Cost Center Accounting); ICH Q10; ISPE Cost of Goods guidance

description: Timestamp when the assay master record was first created in the ELN or data platform. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance and data lineage tracking.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); ICH Q10; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

description: Name of the external Contract Research Organization (CRO) executing this assay when outsourced_to_cro is true. Null for in-house assays. Used for vendor performance tracking, contract management, and regulatory audit trail documentation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM (Vendor Master); ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312

description: Physical or chemical detection principle used to measure the assay signal (e.g., fluorescence, luminescence, radioactivity, mass spectrometry). Distinct from technology_platform — platform is the instrument system, detection_method is the underlying measurement principle. Used for assay validation documentation and GLP compliance records. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fluorescence|luminescence|absorbance|radioactivity|mass_spectrometry|NMR|SPR|calorimetry — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance

description: Identifier of the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) experiment or notebook entry in IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics where the assay development and validation data are recorded. Provides direct traceability from the data product to the source scientific record.
reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics ELN; 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP)

description: Date when the assay was first deployed for compound screening or profiling activities. Marks the operational start of the assay lifecycle. Used for assay age tracking, periodic revalidation scheduling, and portfolio lifecycle management.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook audit trail

description: Operational format describing how the assay is run in the screening workflow (e.g., High-Throughput Screening (HTS) primary screen, dose-response, selectivity panel). Determines throughput capacity planning and compound consumption requirements.
reference: ISPE GAMP 5; IDBS E-WorkBook assay format taxonomy; ICH Q2(R1)

description: Indicates whether the assay is conducted under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations as required for regulatory submissions (IND/NDA/BLA). GLP-compliant assays require full audit trails, validated equipment, and certified personnel. Critical for preclinical safety study data submitted to FDA/EMA.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); OECD Principles of GLP; EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

description: Unit of measurement for the hit_threshold_value (e.g., percent inhibition, nM IC50). Ensures unambiguous interpretation of the hit-calling criterion across different assay types and readout formats.
reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics; ICH Q2(R1); IUPAC nomenclature

description: Numerical threshold used to classify a compound as a 'hit' in primary screening (e.g., ≥ 50% inhibition at 10 µM). Defined during assay validation and used by automated hit-calling algorithms in the HTS data analysis pipeline. Critical for hit-to-lead progression decisions.
reference: IDBS E-WorkBook / Dotmatics hit-calling configuration; ICH Q2(R1); FDA HTS Guidance

description: Standard incubation duration in hours for the assay reaction or cell treatment step. Critical for assay reproducibility and scheduling of automated liquid handling workflows. Stored from the validated assay protocol.
reference: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook protocol parameters; ISPE GAMP 5

description: Date of the most recent formal validation or requalification of the assay per ICH Q2(R1) or fit-for-purpose qualification criteria. Used to trigger periodic revalidation workflows and to assess whether assay data is current for regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH Q2(R1); 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Assay ID
description: Cross-reference identifier for this assay in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) — LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager. Enables bidirectional traceability between the discovery data product and the LIMS assay execution records.
reference: LabWare LIMS / Thermo Fisher SampleManager; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH Q10

description: Indicates whether the assay measures multiple analytes or endpoints simultaneously in a single well or reaction (multiplexed assay). Multiplexed assays increase data density per compound and reduce reagent consumption. Relevant for assay cost modeling and data analysis pipeline configuration.
reference: ICH Q2(R1); IDBS E-WorkBook multiplex assay configuration; LabWare LIMS

business_glossary_term: Outsourced to Contract Research Organization (CRO) Flag
description: Indicates whether this assay is currently outsourced to an external Contract Research Organization (CRO) for execution. When true, the cro_vendor_name field captures the CRO identity. Impacts data governance, IP ownership, and regulatory audit trail requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312; FDA Guidance on Oversight of Clinical Investigations (adapted for preclinical CRO oversight)

description: Name of the research department or functional group that owns and maintains the assay (e.g., 'HTS Group', 'In Vitro Pharmacology', 'ADME Sciences', 'Toxicology'). Used for resource allocation, cost center attribution, and assay portfolio governance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO (Cost Center Management); IDBS E-WorkBook organizational hierarchy

description: Microplate format used in the assay (e.g., 96-well, 384-well, 1536-well). Determines reagent volumes, automation compatibility, and throughput capacity. Critical for liquid handling robot programming and compound dispensing protocols.
reference: ANSI/SLAS Microplate Standards; ISPE GAMP 5; LabWare LIMS plate management

description: Document identifier or URL reference to the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) or assay protocol document stored in the ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics) or document management system (Veeva Vault QualityDocs). Ensures traceability from assay execution to the governing protocol version.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); Veeva Vault QualityDocs; ISPE GAMP 5; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System

description: Version number of the assay protocol document in effect at the time of assay execution (e.g., v1.0, v2.3). Required for GLP audit trails and regulatory submission traceability. Distinct from protocol_reference which is the document identifier.
reference: 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); ICH Q10; Veeva Vault QualityDocs version control

description: Primary quantitative output metric reported by the assay (e.g., IC50, EC50, Ki, Kd, percent inhibition, percent activation). Determines how compound activity data is interpreted in SAR analysis and hit-to-lead progression decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IC50|EC50|Ki|Kd|percent_inhibition|percent_activation|ratio|count|viability_pct — promote to reference product]
reference: IUPAC pharmacology nomenclature; ChEMBL data standards; ICH M10

description: Indicates whether assay results generated using this assay are eligible for inclusion in regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA). Eligibility requires full validation per ICH Q2(R1) and GLP compliance where applicable. Governs data governance workflows for regulatory data packages.
reference: 21 CFR Part 312 (IND); 21 CFR Part 314 (NDA); ICH Q2(R1); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation

description: Date when the assay was formally retired and removed from active use. Null for active assays. Retirement is triggered by target deprioritization, supersession by a superior assay, or platform decommissioning. Required for data governance and historical data archival.
reference: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); IDBS E-WorkBook lifecycle management

description: Ratio of the maximum signal (positive control) to the minimum signal (negative control), quantifying the dynamic range of the assay. A signal window ≥ 2 is typically required for HTS qualification. Used in assay validation reports and Z-factor calculations.
reference: ICH Q2(R1); Zhang JH et al. (1999) SLAS Discovery — Z-factor definition; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance

description: Biological species from which the assay target, cells, or biological material is derived (e.g., human, mouse, rat, recombinant). Critical for translational relevance assessment and cross-species selectivity profiling. Impacts regulatory acceptability of preclinical data for IND submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: human|mouse|rat|rabbit|dog|monkey|in_vitro_recombinant — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: ICH S5(R3) Reproductive Toxicology; ICH S7A/S7B; FDA IND Guidance

description: Detection technology or instrument platform used to execute the assay (e.g., HTRF, AlphaScreen, Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR), NMR, FRET, TR-FRET, Luminescence, Flow Cytometry). Critical for assay reproducibility assessment and equipment scheduling. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HTRF|AlphaScreen|SPR|NMR|FRET|TR-FRET|luminescence|flow_cytometry|mass_spectrometry|fluorescence_polarization — promote to reference product]
reference: ISPE GAMP 5; ICH Q2(R1); LabWare LIMS instrument registry

description: Standard incubation or reaction temperature in degrees Celsius for the assay. Critical for assay reproducibility across sites and instruments. Deviations from this value are flagged as out-of-specification (OOS) events in the LIMS.
reference: ICH Q2(R1); 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); LabWare LIMS environmental monitoring

description: Disease or therapeutic area that the assay supports (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience, Cardiovascular). Links assay activity to the business portfolio and pipeline planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_diseases|neuroscience|cardiovascular|infectious_diseases|metabolic — promote to reference product]
reference: WHO ICD-11; ATC classification; ICH E8(R1) General Considerations for Clinical Studies

description: Maximum number of compounds or samples that can be processed per day using this assay under standard HTS conditions. Serves as the MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used for compound library screening campaign planning and resource scheduling in the discovery lab.
reference: ISPE GAMP 5; IDBS E-WorkBook capacity planning module

description: Current lifecycle state of the assay with respect to its scientific and regulatory validation. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. 'validated' indicates full ICH Q2(R1) compliance; 'qualified' indicates fit-for-purpose qualification; 'development' indicates the assay is still being optimized. Governs whether assay results can be used in regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH Q2(R1) Validation of Analytical Procedures; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP); FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance 2018

description: Statistical measure of assay quality (Z') calculated from positive and negative control variability. Values ≥ 0.5 indicate an excellent assay suitable for HTS. Stored as the validated Z' from the assay qualification run. Used to gate assay deployment for compound screening campaigns.
reference: Zhang JH et al. (1999) A Simple Statistical Parameter for Use in Evaluation and Validation of High Throughput Screening Assays; ICH Q2(R1)

description: PubMed Identifier (PMID) or Digital Object Identifier (DOI) for literature-sourced ICSRs. Populated when report_type = 'literature'. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.4.r.1. Supports systematic literature review (SLR) traceability.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.4.r.1; GVP Module VI B.2; ICH E2D

description: Indicates whether the ICSR meets the four ICH E2B minimum criteria for a valid case: (1) identifiable reporter, (2) identifiable patient, (3) suspect drug, (4) adverse event. Cases not meeting minimum criteria are tracked but not submitted. Corresponds to ICH E2D minimum information requirements.
reference: ICH E2D; ICH E2B(R3); GVP Module VI B.1

description: Date of the most recent follow-up information received for this case, resetting the regulatory clock for follow-up submissions. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.5.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.5; GVP Module VI B.4

description: Unit of measurement for patient_age_value. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) D.2.2b. Supports neonatal and pediatric cases where age is expressed in days, weeks, or months.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) D.2.2b; ICH E11 (Pediatric Studies)

description: De-identified patient age at the time of the adverse event onset, expressed as a numeric value. Must be used in conjunction with patient_age_unit. Stored per GDPR/HIPAA de-identification standards. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) D.2.2a.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) D.2.2a; GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; GVP Module VI

description: Biological sex of the patient as reported. De-identified demographic field per GDPR/HIPAA. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) D.5. Used in signal detection and benefit-risk assessment stratification.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) D.5; GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164

description: Patient body weight in kilograms at the time of the adverse event, as reported. De-identified per GDPR/HIPAA. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) D.3. Used for dose-weight relationship analysis in signal detection.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) D.3; GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164

business_glossary_term: Primary Adverse Event MedDRA Preferred Term (PT)
description: MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) Preferred Term (PT) coding for the primary adverse event/reaction reported. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) E.i.2.1b. Standardized coding enables cross-case signal detection and regulatory submission.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) E.i.2.1b; MedDRA; ICH M1; GVP Module VI

business_glossary_term: Primary Adverse Event MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC)
description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) for the primary adverse event, derived from the MedDRA PT hierarchy. Supports aggregate signal detection by organ system and PSUR/PBRER tabulation requirements.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) E.i.2.1a; MedDRA; ICH E2C(R2) PBRER; GVP Module VII

description: Date the ICSR was first received by the company (MAH/sponsor), establishing the regulatory clock start date (Day 0) for 7-day expedited and 15-day expedited reporting obligations. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.4.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.4; 21 CFR Part 314.81(b)(1); GVP Module VI B.4

description: Outcome of rechallenge — whether the adverse event recurred upon re-administration of the suspect drug after dechallenge. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.3b. Strengthens causality evidence and is critical for SUSAR assessment in clinical trials.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.3b; ICH E2A; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment

description: Calculated deadline date by which the ICSR must be submitted to the relevant health authority (FDA, EMA, PMDA, NMPA, TGA). Derived from receipt_date plus applicable reporting window (7 or 15 calendar days for expedited reports; 90 days for non-expedited). SLA-critical field for compliance monitoring.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314.81(b)(1); GVP Module VI B.4; ICH E2A; PMDA Pharmacovigilance Regulations

description: Current submission status of the ICSR to the applicable health authority. Tracks compliance against 7-day and 15-day expedited reporting deadlines. Overdue status triggers escalation per PV SLA management procedures.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314.81(b)(1); GVP Module VI B.4; ICH E2A; PMDA Pharmacovigilance Regulations

description: Classification of the ICSR source channel per ICH E2B(R3) C.1.3. Drives regulatory reporting obligations and processing workflows. Spontaneous reports from HCPs/patients, literature-sourced cases (PMID/DOI), clinical trial SAEs, solicited reports from patient support programs, and other sources.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.3; 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module VI

description: Internal case number assigned by the company (MAH/sponsor) in the source system (Argus Safety / Oracle AERS). Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.8.1. Used for internal tracking and reconciliation with the worldwide unique case ID.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.8.1; Argus Safety Case Number

description: Indicates whether the adverse event meets ICH E2A seriousness criteria (death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, congenital anomaly, or medically significant). True = Serious Adverse Event (SAE). Drives expedited 7-day or 15-day regulatory reporting obligation. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) E.i.3.2.
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) E.i.3.2; 21 CFR Part 312.32; GVP Module VI B.3

description: Specific ICH E2A seriousness criterion or criteria met by the adverse event. Multiple criteria may apply. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) E.i.3.2a-f. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) E.i.3.2a-f; 21 CFR Part 312.32

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the adverse event occurred. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.17.1. Determines applicable regulatory authority for submission routing (FDA, EMA, PMDA, NMPA, TGA, MHRA).
reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.17.1; ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; GVP Module VI

business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Flag
description: Indicates whether the case qualifies as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) — i.e., serious, unexpected (unlisted), and with a reasonable causal relationship to the investigational medicinal product. True = SUSAR requiring 7-day (fatal/life-threatening) or 15-day expedited reporting to health authorities and ethics committees.
reference: ICH E2A; 21 CFR Part 312.32(c); EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; GVP Module VI

description: Medical indication (disease/condition) for which the suspect drug was prescribed or used, coded using MedDRA terminology. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) G.k.7.r.2b. Supports benefit-risk assessment and signal contextualization.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) G.k.7.r.2b; MedDRA; GVP Module VI

description: Primary health authority to which this ICSR must be submitted. Determined by source_country_code and product registration status. Drives submission format selection (MedWatch 3500A, EudraVigilance E2B, J-ICSR, NMPA XML). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|PMDA|NMPA|MHRA|TGA|WHO|ANVISA|Health_Canada|other — promote to reference product]
reference: 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance; PMDA E2B(R3) Implementation Guide; NMPA ADR Reporting Regulations

description: Globally unique case identifier assigned at intake, conforming to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.1 format (sender identifier + case number). Used for cross-regional deduplication and regulatory submission tracking across FDA MedWatch, EudraVigilance, J-ICSR, and NMPA.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) C.1.1; 21 CFR Part 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance Technical Specification

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each adverse reaction record within the pharmacovigilance system. Primary key for the pv_adverse_reaction data product in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); 21 CFR Part 314; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance

description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.atc_classification. Business justification: Linking adverse reactions to ATC therapeutic class enables signal detection by drug category, benefit-risk analysis, and PSUR aggregate reporting. Medical coding teams perform MedDRA-to-ATC cross-tabu

Foreign key linking to commercial.brand. Business justification: Adverse reactions aggregated by brand for safety surveillance, label update decisions, and competitive safety positioning. Essential for brand risk management committees and periodic benefit-risk eval

Reference to the parent Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) to which this adverse reaction belongs. One ICSR may contain multiple adverse reaction records. Supports header-detail navigation for case processing.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety

description: Reference to the suspect medicinal product (drug product) associated with this adverse reaction. Links to the master product record for the drug under pharmacovigilance surveillance.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) B.4; FDA NDA/BLA; EMA EudraVigilance product dictionary; Argus Safety product field

description: Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.rsi. Business justification: Listedness determination for adverse reactions uses RSI (Reference Safety Information) as the authoritative source. Add rsi_id FK to link to the specific RSI version used for assessment. Remove rsi_do

Action taken with the suspect medicinal product in response to the adverse reaction: dose reduced, drug withdrawn, dose not changed, not applicable, unknown, or dose increased. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.4.k.8 and is required for regulatory ICSR submissions.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) B.4.k.8; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety action taken

description: Free-text medical narrative describing the clinical course of this adverse reaction, including relevant medical history, concomitant medications, treatment, and outcome. Required for regulatory ICSR submissions and medical review. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field H.1.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) H.1; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety narrative field

description: Assessment of the causal relationship between the suspect drug and the adverse reaction, using WHO-UMC or company standard causality categories. Drives listedness determination, SUSAR classification, and signal detection weighting.
reference: WHO-UMC Causality Assessment System; ICH E2B(R3) B.4.k.18; FDA MedWatch; Argus Safety causality

description: The methodology or algorithm used to perform the causality assessment (e.g., WHO-UMC scale, Naranjo algorithm, company-specific algorithm). Supports audit trail and methodological consistency across cases.
reference: WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; Naranjo Algorithm; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety

description: User identifier of the medical coder or system process that performed or confirmed the MedDRA coding. Required for audit trail under 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance. Stores the user login or system account name.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Argus Safety audit trail; EMA EudraVigilance

description: Date on which the MedDRA coding was completed for this adverse reaction. Used for coding turnaround time metrics, audit trail, and compliance with regulatory submission timelines.
reference: MedDRA Term Selection: Points to Consider; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Indicates whether the MedDRA coding was performed automatically by the safety system (auto-coded), manually by a medical coder (manual review), or auto-coded and subsequently confirmed by manual review. Supports coding quality metrics and audit trail requirements.
reference: MedDRA Term Selection: Points to Consider; ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety coding workflow; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Timestamp when this adverse reaction record was first created in the pharmacovigilance safety database. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VI. Supports case processing timeline metrics.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety audit trail

business_glossary_term: Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade
description: Severity grade assigned per the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE), ranging from 1 (mild) to 5 (death). Applicable primarily for oncology clinical trial adverse events. Null for non-oncology or post-market cases where CTCAE grading is not applicable.
reference: NCI CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Oncology guidance; Medidata Rave CTCAE grading

description: Outcome of dechallenge (withdrawal of the suspect drug) on the adverse reaction. Positive dechallenge (reaction improved or resolved after withdrawal) supports causality. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.4.k.18.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) B.4.k.18; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; Argus Safety dechallenge field

description: Indicates whether this adverse reaction meets the regulatory definition of a Serious Adverse Event (SAE) per ICH E2A criteria. True if any seriousness criterion is met. Drives expedited reporting timelines (7-day or 15-day) to health authorities.
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.3; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance; 21 CFR Part 314

business_glossary_term: Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) Indicator
description: Indicates whether this adverse reaction has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR). True when the reaction is serious, unexpected (unlisted), and there is a reasonable causal relationship to the investigational medicinal product. Triggers mandatory expedited reporting to health authorities and ethics committees.
reference: ICH E2A; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA SUSAR reporting guideline

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this adverse reaction record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11. Used to track follow-up updates and case amendments in the safety database.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety audit trail

description: Determination of whether this adverse reaction is listed (expected) or unlisted (unexpected) in the current Reference Safety Information (RSI), such as the Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS) or Investigator Brochure (IB). Unlisted serious reactions in clinical trials constitute Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) requiring expedited reporting.
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2D; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA SUSAR reporting guideline; Argus Safety listedness

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) High Level Group Term (HLGT) Code
description: MedDRA High Level Group Term (HLGT) code, one level above HLT in the MedDRA hierarchy. Supports broader therapeutic area grouping for signal detection and regulatory submissions.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2C(R2)

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) High Level Term (HLT) Code
description: MedDRA High Level Term (HLT) code representing the grouping level above the Preferred Term. Used for aggregate signal detection and periodic safety update report (PSUR) tabulations.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3); ICH E2C(R2) PSUR

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Code
description: MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) numeric code assigned to this adverse reaction after coding. The PT is the primary level used for regulatory reporting, signal detection, and line listing generation. Mandatory for ICSR submissions to FDA and EMA.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.2a; EMA EudraVigilance; FDA MedWatch

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Preferred Term (PT) Name
description: Human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) label corresponding to the meddra_pt_code. Stored denormalized for reporting and line listing generation without requiring a join to the MedDRA reference table.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.2b

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) System Organ Class (SOC) Code
description: MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code representing the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy. Used for regulatory line listings, PSUR summary tabulations, and risk management plan (RMP) categorization.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.2c; ICH E2C(R2); EMA RMP guideline

business_glossary_term: Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) Version
description: Version of the MedDRA dictionary used to code this adverse reaction (e.g., 26.0, 26.1). Critical for regulatory submissions and recoding exercises when MedDRA versions are updated. Required for reproducibility of signal detection analyses.
reference: MedDRA Introductory Guide; ICH E2B(R3); EMA EudraVigilance technical specification

description: Indicates whether the adverse reaction has been medically confirmed by a healthcare professional (HCP). Medically confirmed cases carry greater weight in signal detection and regulatory reporting. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field A.1.7.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.7; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety

description: Date on which the adverse reaction first began. Used to calculate time-to-onset from drug exposure, supports causality assessment, and is required for ICSR regulatory submissions. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.2.i.4.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.4; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety

description: Standardized outcome of the adverse reaction at the time of reporting. Values align with ICH E2B(R3) outcome codes: recovered/resolved, recovering/resolving, not recovered/not resolved, fatal, unknown, recovered with sequelae. Mandatory for regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.7; FDA MedWatch; EMA EudraVigilance; Argus Safety outcome field

description: Duration of the adverse reaction in days, calculated from onset to resolution. Stored as a business attribute when explicitly reported by the reporter or calculated during case processing. Supports time-to-resolution analytics and benefit-risk assessments.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.5; Argus Safety duration field; ICH E2C(R2) PSUR

description: Sequential line number of this adverse reaction within the parent ICSR, enabling ordering and identification of multiple events within a single case. Corresponds to the reaction/event sequence in ICH E2B(R3) message structure.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) Section B.2; Argus Safety reaction sequence

description: Current workflow processing status of this adverse reaction record within the pharmacovigilance case management system: new (received, not yet processed), under review, coded (MedDRA coding complete), medically reviewed, closed (finalized), or deleted (voided). Drives case management workflow in Argus Safety.
reference: EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; Argus Safety case workflow; ICH E2B(R3)

description: Outcome of rechallenge (re-administration of the suspect drug after withdrawal) if performed. Positive rechallenge (reaction recurred) strengthens causality. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.4.k.19.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) B.4.k.19; WHO-UMC Causality Assessment; Argus Safety rechallenge field

description: Classification of the regulatory reporting obligation triggered by this adverse reaction: 7-day expedited (unexpected fatal/life-threatening SUSAR), 15-day expedited (other serious unexpected), periodic (PSUR/PBRER), non-expedited, or not reportable. Drives submission workflow and deadline tracking.
reference: ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance; EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014; ICH E2C(R2)

description: Classification of the original source from which this adverse reaction was reported: spontaneous (unsolicited), clinical trial, published literature, regulatory authority, or other. Determines applicable reporting timelines and regulatory obligations. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field A.1.4.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.1.4; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; EMA EudraVigilance; ICH E2D

description: Date on which the adverse reaction resolved or ended. Null if the event is ongoing, fatal, or outcome is unknown. Used to calculate event duration and supports outcome determination. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.2.i.6.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.6; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; Argus Safety

description: Pipe-delimited list of applicable seriousness criteria met by this adverse reaction per ICH E2A: death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability/incapacity, congenital anomaly, medically significant. Supports regulatory reporting classification and expedited reporting decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|prolonged_hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]
reference: ICH E2A; ICH E2B(R3) B.1.i.3; FDA 21 CFR 312.32; EMA EudraVigilance

description: Narrative severity classification of the adverse reaction using standard WHO/ICH terminology: mild, moderate, severe, life-threatening, or fatal. Complements CTCAE grade for non-oncology cases and post-market surveillance where CTCAE grading is not used.
reference: WHO Adverse Reaction Terminology; ICH E2B(R3); FDA MedWatch; Argus Safety severity field

description: Indicates whether this adverse reaction record has been flagged as contributing to a potential pharmacovigilance signal under review. Set by the signal detection process in the safety database. Supports signal management workflow and regulatory signal reporting obligations.
reference: ICH E2C(R2); EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP) Module IX; FDA Pharmacovigilance guidance

description: Number of days from the first dose of the suspect drug to the onset of the adverse reaction. A key pharmacovigilance metric used in signal detection, causality assessment, and benefit-risk evaluation. Derived from drug start date and reaction onset date during case processing.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); WHO-UMC Signal Detection; FDA Pharmacovigilance guidance; Argus Safety

description: The exact adverse event term as reported by the original reporter (patient, healthcare professional, or literature source) before MedDRA coding. Preserved verbatim for coding audit trail and signal detection. Required per ICH E2B(R3) field B.2.i.1.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) B.2.i.1; FDA 21 CFR 314.81; Argus Safety verbatim term

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the pharmacovigilance reporter record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for the reporter master data entity.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Entity

description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Reporter country determines follow-up feasibility, data privacy regulations (GDPR vs others), contact protocols, and language requirements. Operational necessity for case management and regulatory com

Foreign key linking to compliance.debarment_check. Business justification: Reporters (especially clinical investigators) must be screened against FDA debarment and OIG exclusion lists per GCP requirements. Debarment screening is mandatory for investigator qualification and o

Foreign key linking to hcp.hcp_master. Business justification: When reporter is HCP (is_hcp flag), linking to hcp_master enables license verification, specialty validation for causality assessment, NPI matching for regulatory submissions, and structured follow-up

Reference to the canonical/master reporter record when this record has been identified as a duplicate. Null if this record is itself the master. Supports deduplication and case re-linking workflows in the PV system.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Duplicate Management

description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.address. Business justification: Structured address linkage enables standardized contact management, duplicate reporter detection, and GDPR compliance (right to erasure). Replaces fragmented address fields with master data reference

Privacy-compliant pseudonymous identifier assigned to the reporter in lieu of personal identifiers, enabling case aggregation and follow-up management without exposing PII. Mandatory under GDPR and HIPAA for PV processing.
reference: GDPR Article 4 & Article 25; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514; ICH E2B(R3) A.1.7

description: Source system identifier for the reporter as assigned by Argus Safety / Oracle AERS. Used for lineage tracing and deduplication against the operational PV system.
reference: Argus Safety / Oracle AERS Reporter Master; ICH E2B(R3) A.1.7

description: Date on which the reporter provided or withdrew consent to be contacted for follow-up. Required for GDPR audit trail demonstrating lawful basis for processing personal data.

Indicates whether the reporter has provided explicit consent to be contacted for follow-up queries regarding the adverse event report. Mandatory consent gate under GDPR Article 7 before any follow-up communication is initiated.
reference: GDPR Article 7; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.508; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

description: Preferred channel for follow-up communication as indicated by the reporter. Drives the follow-up workflow in Argus Safety. 'no_contact' indicates the reporter has declined further contact, which must be respected per GDPR consent obligations.
reference: GDPR Article 7; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; Argus Safety Follow-up Workflow

description: Timestamp when the reporter record was first created in the PV system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records in regulated pharmaceutical environments.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; GDPR Article 30

description: Department or unit within the reporter's organization (e.g., Oncology Ward, Clinical Pharmacology, Drug Safety). Supports routing of follow-up queries to the correct organizational unit.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.4; Argus Safety Reporter Master

description: Indicates whether this reporter record has been identified as a potential or confirmed duplicate of another reporter record. Duplicate reporters must be resolved before case processing to prevent double-counting in aggregate safety analyses.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; Argus Safety Duplicate Detection

description: Primary email address of the reporter for electronic follow-up correspondence. Classified as restricted PII. Used only for PV case follow-up; not shared with commercial systems. Consent-gated per GDPR.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.6; GDPR Article 4 & Article 6; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

description: Last/family name of the individual reporter. Stored in restricted classification per GDPR and HIPAA. Used for follow-up correspondence and duplicate detection. May be withheld or anonymized per reporter consent.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.3b; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

description: Fax number of the reporter or their institution, used for formal follow-up correspondence in jurisdictions where fax remains a regulatory-accepted communication channel (e.g., Japan PMDA submissions).
reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.6; PMDA Pharmacovigilance Guidelines

description: Date on which the reporter submitted their first adverse event report to the company. Used for longitudinal reporter relationship analysis and tenure-based reliability assessment.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Master; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Target date by which a follow-up response from the reporter is required to meet regulatory submission timelines (e.g., 15-day expedited reporting for SUSARs and SAEs). Calculated based on initial receipt date and applicable regulatory clock.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); FDA 21 CFR §312.32; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 314.81

description: Indicates whether outstanding follow-up queries have been sent to this reporter and a response is pending. Drives the follow-up management workflow in Argus Safety to ensure timely case completion within regulatory timeframes.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI; FDA 21 CFR §312.32; Argus Safety Follow-up Workflow

description: Date on which the GDPR Right to Erasure request was processed and PII fields were anonymized. Null if no erasure request has been received. Required for GDPR compliance audit trail.
reference: GDPR Article 17 & Article 30; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Indicates whether the reporter has submitted a Right to Erasure (Right to be Forgotten) request under GDPR Article 17. When true, PII fields must be anonymized while retaining the anonymized case record for pharmacovigilance regulatory obligations under GDPR Article 17(3)(c).
reference: GDPR Article 17; EMA GVP Module VI; ICH E2B(R3)

description: First/given name of the individual reporter. Stored in restricted classification per GDPR and HIPAA. Used for follow-up correspondence and duplicate detection. May be withheld or anonymized per reporter consent.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.3a; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA 45 CFR §164.514

description: Indicates whether the reporter is a qualified Healthcare Professional (HCP). HCP-reported cases carry higher regulatory weight and may trigger expedited 15-day reporting obligations to FDA, EMA, and other health authorities.
reference: ICH E2B(R3) A.2.1.2; FDA 21 CFR §314.81; EMA GVP Module VI; 21 CFR Part 312.32

description: ISO 639-1 or ISO 639-2 language code representing the reporter's preferred communication language. Used to route follow-up correspondence to appropriately qualified multilingual PV staff and to select translated follow-up letter templates.
reference: ISO 639-1; ICH E2B(R3); EMA GVP Module VI

description: Date of the most recent adverse event report submitted by this reporter. Used to identify active versus dormant reporters and to support follow-up prioritization.
reference: ICH E2B(R3); Argus Safety Reporter Master; EMA GVP Module VI

Indicator whether corrective action is required to address identified deficiencies. True indicates Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) plan must be developed and tracked. False indicates no remediation needed.

description: Assessment of residual risk exposure given identified control deficiencies. Critical indicates immediate risk of material financial misstatement or regulatory non-compliance. Number of control instances or transactions tested during the assessment. Indicator whether this control is in scope for SOX 404 management assessment and external auditor attestation. Overall conclusion on control operating effectiveness. Effective indicates control operated as designed with no material exceptions. Ineffective indicates control failures that could result in material misstatement or compliance violation. Not tested indicates assessment planned but not executed. Methodology used to evaluate control effectiveness. Inquiry involves interviewing control performers. Observation involves watching control execution in real-time. Inspection involves examining documentary evidence. Reperformance involves independently executing the control. Walkthrough involves tracing a single transaction end-to-end. Sample testing involves statistical sampling of control instances. Full population testing involves examining all control instances in the period.
