description: Indicates whether postings to this GL account are currently blocked (True) at the company code level. A blocked account prevents new journal entries, used during period-end close or account restructuring.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module — Table SKB1 field XSPEB; SOX Section 404

description: SAP profit center code representing the business unit or therapeutic area (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases) to which the GL balance is allocated. Enables P&L reporting by therapeutic area, brand, and geography.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA Module; IFRS 8 Operating Segments; US GAAP ASC 280

description: Indicates whether the GL account balance is subject to R&D capitalization rules under IFRS IAS 38 (True) or expensed as incurred under US GAAP ASC 730 (False). Critical for pharmaceutical companies managing the boundary between R&D expense and intangible asset capitalization.
reference: IFRS IAS 38 Intangible Assets; US GAAP ASC 730 Research and Development; SOX Section 404

description: Indicates if this GL account is a reconciliation account and its type: D=Accounts Receivable (Customers), K=Accounts Payable (Vendors), A=Assets, or empty for non-reconciliation accounts. Reconciliation accounts aggregate subledger balances into the GL.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module — Table SKB1 field MITKZ; US GAAP ASC 210; IFRS IAS 1

description: Timestamp when this GL account balance record was first created in the Silver layer data product. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and SOX-compliant record-keeping requirements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 302/404; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; GDPR Article 5

description: Timestamp when this GL account balance record was last modified in the Silver layer data product. Supports incremental data loading, change tracking, and SOX-compliant audit trail requirements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 302/404; 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; GDPR Article 5

description: Segment identifier for IFRS 8 / ASC 280 segment reporting (e.g., 'Oncology', 'Immunology', 'Rare Disease', 'Consumer Health'). Enables disaggregated P&L and asset reporting by operating segment for external financial disclosures.
reference: IFRS 8 Operating Segments; US GAAP ASC 280; SAP S/4HANA FI-GL Segment

description: Indicates whether this GL account is in scope for SOX Section 302/404 internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR). SOX-relevant accounts require documented controls, testing, and sign-off during the annual audit cycle.
reference: SOX Section 302 and 404; PCAOB AS 2201; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

description: SAP tax code associated with the GL account for VAT/GST and withholding tax determination. Relevant for pharmaceutical entities operating across multiple tax jurisdictions. Supports indirect tax reporting and compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-TX Module; IFRS IAS 12 Income Taxes; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Company code of the intercompany trading partner for balances involving intercompany transactions. Used to identify and eliminate intercompany balances during group consolidation. Populated only when intercompany_flag is True.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-GL Intercompany — Table FAGLFLEXT field RASSC; IFRS 10; US GAAP ASC 810

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each journal entry record in the general ledger. Primary key for the journal_entry data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; 21 CFR Part 11; SOX Section 302/404

description: Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: Journal entries generated by AP postings should reference the source AP document. This is a nullable FK since not all journal entries are AP-related. Strengthens accounts_payable connections to journa

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Journal entries require audit trail linking posting_user to employee master for SOX compliance, segregation of duties controls, and financial audit requirements. Existing posting_user is username stri

Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: Journal entries related to fixed asset transactions (acquisition, depreciation, disposal, impairment) should reference the specific asset. This is a nullable FK since not all journal entries are asset

Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Journal entries post to specific GL accounts. Each JE line item must reference the GL account it impacts. The existing gl_account field is a STRING code; adding general_ledger_id establishes the prope

Foreign key linking to procurement.goods_receipt. Business justification: Journal entries for inventory receipts and accruals link to goods receipts for inventory accounting audit trail and period-end accrual validation. Essential for pharmaceutical inventory accounting, en

Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Journal entries that charge costs to internal orders should reference the internal order. This is a nullable FK since not all journal entries are internal-order-related. Connects internal_order to jou

Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor_invoice. Business justification: Journal entries for invoice accruals and postings need vendor invoice traceability for audit trail and invoice-to-GL reconciliation. Critical for pharmaceutical financial close processes, SOX complian
Monetary amount of the journal entry translated into the corporate group reporting currency (typically USD or EUR) for consolidated P&L reporting by therapeutic area, brand, and geography.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS 10; IAS 21; SOX Section 302

description: Monetary amount of the journal entry translated into the company code's local (functional) currency using the applicable exchange rate. Used for statutory financial reporting and local tax compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 21; IFRS; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Gross monetary amount of the journal entry in the original transaction currency. For debit entries this is positive; for credit entries this is negative (SAP sign convention). Core monetary fact for the posting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 21; IFRS 15; SOX Section 404

description: SAP assignment field (ZUONR) used for sorting and matching open items in accounts payable, accounts receivable, and bank reconciliation. Typically populated with invoice number, payment reference, or contract number for automated clearing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404

description: SAP business area code representing an organizational unit for which an internal balance sheet and P&L can be drawn up. Used for segment reporting across geographies and therapeutic areas.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS 8; US GAAP ASC 280

description: SAP company code identifying the legal entity for which the journal entry is posted. Enables P&L reporting by legal entity and supports multi-entity consolidation across the pharmaceutical group.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements; SOX Section 302

description: SAP CO cost center to which the expense or revenue is assigned. Enables cost allocation by department, therapeutic area, or function (e.g., R&D, Manufacturing, Commercial). Supports internal P&L and ROI analysis for drug programs.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; IFRS; US GAAP; SOX Section 404

description: SAP indicator specifying whether the line item is a debit (S=Soll/Debit) or credit (H=Haben/Credit) posting. Fundamental double-entry bookkeeping attribute required for GL balance validation and trial balance generation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS; US GAAP; Double-Entry Bookkeeping Principles

description: The date of the original source document (invoice date, payment date, contract date) that triggered the journal entry. May differ from posting_date; used for aging analysis and vendor/customer terms calculation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 1; IFRS 15

description: SAP-assigned unique accounting document number within the company code and fiscal year. Serves as the externally-known business identifier for the journal entry, used in audit trails and reconciliation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11

description: SAP document type code classifying the nature of the journal entry (e.g., SA=General Ledger, KR=Vendor Invoice, DR=Customer Invoice, AA=Asset Posting, ZP=Payment Clearing, ML=Material Ledger). Drives posting rules and account determination. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SA|KR|DR|AA|ZP|ML|AB|KZ|DZ|WA|WE|RE — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS; US GAAP

description: The exact date and time when the journal entry record was created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under SOX and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; 21 CFR Part 11; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

description: Foreign currency exchange rate applied to translate the transaction currency amount to local currency at the time of posting. Sourced from SAP exchange rate tables per the applicable rate type (e.g., M=standard, B=bank buying rate).
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 21; ECB exchange rate guidelines

description: The fiscal period (month 01–12, plus special periods 13–16 for year-end adjustments) within the fiscal year. Drives period-end close processes, P&L reporting by period, and financial close calendar management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 34 Interim Financial Reporting; SOX Section 404

description: The fiscal year to which the journal entry belongs, as defined in the SAP fiscal year variant. Used for annual financial reporting, R&D capitalization tracking, and SOX compliance period assignment.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 1; US GAAP ASC 270

description: SAP functional area classifying the business function of the posting (e.g., R&D, Manufacturing, Sales & Distribution, General & Administrative). Supports cost-of-goods-sold (COGS) analysis and functional P&L reporting per IFRS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: R&D|Manufacturing|Sales|Marketing|G&A|Regulatory|Medical Affairs|Supply Chain — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; IFRS; US GAAP ASC 730; SOX Section 404

description: SAP GL account number to which the journal entry line is posted. Determines the financial statement line item (P&L or balance sheet). Supports COGS by product, R&D capitalization, and therapeutic area P&L analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; US GAAP ASC 730 (R&D); IFRS; SOX Section 404

description: Free-text description at the journal entry header level explaining the business purpose of the posting (e.g., 'Q3 R&D accrual – Oncology Phase III', 'API procurement – CMO settlement'). Supports audit review and financial close documentation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Indicates whether this journal entry is itself a reversal of a prior posting (True) or an original entry (False). Used to filter reversals from net financial reporting and to identify accrual reversal patterns in period-end close.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404; IFRS; US GAAP

description: The date and time when the journal entry was last modified or reversed. Supports change audit trail requirements under SOX Section 404 and 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records integrity.
reference: SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

description: Sequential line item number within the journal entry document (e.g., 001, 002). Uniquely identifies each debit/credit line within the document for reconciliation, audit, and subledger matching.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Free-text description at the individual line item level providing context for the specific debit or credit posting (e.g., 'API batch #XYZ123 – COGS', 'Phase III trial accrual – CRO milestone'). Supports granular audit review.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the company code's local (functional) currency. Used for statutory reporting in the country of the legal entity.
reference: ISO 4217; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 21; IFRS

description: The date on which the journal entry is posted to the general ledger. Determines the fiscal period and year to which the transaction is assigned. Critical for period-end close and financial reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 1 Presentation of Financial Statements; SOX Section 404

description: Current workflow state of the journal entry in the general ledger lifecycle. 'posted' = fully committed to GL; 'parked' = saved but not posted; 'held' = incomplete draft; 'reversed' = offset entry created; 'cleared' = matched against open items; 'blocked' = pending approval.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404; IFRS

description: SAP CO profit center representing the business unit or product line responsible for the financial result. Enables P&L reporting by therapeutic area (oncology, immunology, rare diseases), brand, and geography.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; IFRS 8 Operating Segments; SOX Section 404

description: External reference number from the source document (e.g., vendor invoice number, purchase order number, contract reference, or regulatory submission reference). Enables cross-system reconciliation and audit traceability.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Document number of the reversing journal entry if this posting has been reversed. Populated only for reversed entries; null otherwise. Supports audit trail completeness and period-end close validation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11; IFRS

description: Identifies the subledger from which the journal entry originates: AP (Accounts Payable), AR (Accounts Receivable), asset accounting, tax accounting, material ledger, or none (direct GL posting). Enables subledger-to-GL reconciliation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IFRS; US GAAP; SOX Section 404

description: The calculated tax amount (VAT, GST, sales tax) in local currency for the journal entry line. Supports indirect tax return filing, tax provision calculations, and multi-jurisdiction tax compliance reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; US IRC; OECD BEPS; SOX Section 404

description: The taxable base amount in local currency on which the tax is calculated. Required for indirect tax return preparation and multi-jurisdiction VAT/GST compliance reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; OECD BEPS; US IRC

description: SAP tax code identifying the applicable tax rate and type (e.g., VAT, sales tax, withholding tax) for the posting. Drives automatic tax calculation and links to tax jurisdiction for multi-jurisdiction indirect tax compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; 21 CFR Part 11; OECD BEPS

description: Code identifying the tax jurisdiction (country, state, county, city) applicable to the transaction for multi-jurisdiction indirect tax reporting. Required for US sales tax (Vertex/Avalara integration) and international VAT compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; US IRC; EU VAT Directive; OECD BEPS; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The reporting period (YYYY-MM) to which this tax posting belongs for indirect tax return filing purposes. May differ from the accounting fiscal period; used for VAT/GST return preparation across multiple tax jurisdictions.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; HMRC VAT regulations; OECD BEPS

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the original transaction (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY, GBP). The currency in which the business transaction was originally denominated, before conversion to local or group currency.
reference: ISO 4217; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 21 Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates

description: Classification of the tax posting type for indirect tax reporting: input VAT (recoverable on purchases), output VAT (collected on sales), deferred VAT (timing difference), exempt, zero-rated, or not applicable. Supports multi-jurisdiction VAT compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; HMRC; OECD BEPS

description: Amount of withholding tax (WHT) deducted at source for cross-border payments to vendors, royalty recipients, or service providers. Relevant for pharmaceutical royalty accounting, CRO/CMO payments, and international tax treaty compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; OECD Model Tax Convention; US IRC Section 1441; BEPS Action 6

description: Primary key for ledger
Reference to the chart of accounts structure used by this ledger. Defines the complete list of general ledger accounts available for posting.
Self-referencing FK on ledger (parent_ledger_id)
The accounting standard or principle governing this ledger (e.g., US GAAP, IFRS, local statutory GAAP, tax accounting, management accounting). Determines valuation, recognition, and disclosure rules.
Indicates whether this ledger supports profit and loss reporting segmented by pharmaceutical brand or product line. True if brand dimension is enabled, False otherwise.
Indicates whether this ledger tracks cost of goods sold by product for pharmaceutical manufacturing and distribution. True if COGS tracking is enabled, False otherwise.

Identifier of the legal entity or company code to which this ledger belongs. Represents the smallest organizational unit for which a complete self-contained set of accounts can be drawn up for external reporting.

Indicates whether this ledger is used for group consolidation purposes. Consolidation ledgers aggregate financial data from multiple legal entities for consolidated financial statements. True if consolidation ledger, False otherwise.
The date and time when this ledger record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code representing the functional currency of the ledger (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, JPY). All transactions in this ledger are recorded in this currency.
Detailed textual description of the ledger's purpose, scope, and usage. Provides context for financial analysts and auditors on when and how this ledger should be used.
The date on which this ledger ceases to be active for new postings. Nullable for ledgers with no planned end date. Used for ledger retirement or fiscal year transitions.
The date from which this ledger becomes active and available for financial postings. Represents the beginning of the ledger's operational lifecycle.
Code identifying the fiscal year calendar structure used by this ledger (e.g., calendar year, April-March, custom periods). Defines period start/end dates and number of posting periods.
Indicates whether this ledger supports profit and loss reporting segmented by geographic region or country. True if geography dimension is enabled, False otherwise.

Indicates whether this is the leading (primary) ledger for the organization. The leading ledger is the authoritative source for statutory financial reporting and consolidation. True if leading ledger, False otherwise.
Unique alphanumeric code identifying the ledger in financial systems. Used as the business identifier for external references and reporting.
Full descriptive name of the ledger (e.g., 'Corporate General Ledger', 'IFRS Reporting Ledger', 'Management Accounting Ledger').

Classification of the ledger based on its accounting purpose. General ledgers capture all financial transactions; subsidiary ledgers track specific account categories; statistical ledgers hold non-financial data; special purpose ledgers support specific reporting requirements; consolidation ledgers aggregate multi-entity data; management ledgers support internal decision-making.
User identifier or system account that last modified this ledger record. Supports audit trail and accountability for ledger configuration changes.
The date and time when this ledger record was last modified. Supports audit trail and change tracking for ledger configuration changes.

Indicates whether this ledger is part of a parallel accounting setup, where multiple ledgers track the same transactions under different accounting principles (e.g., GAAP and IFRS). True if parallel ledger, False otherwise.

Indicates whether financial postings are currently allowed to this ledger. Used to control posting periods and prevent unauthorized entries during period-end close. True if postings allowed, False otherwise.
General ledger account number used to accumulate net profit or loss for the current period in this ledger. Cleared to retained earnings during year-end close.
Indicates whether this ledger tracks capitalized research and development costs for pharmaceutical development programs. True if R&D capitalization is tracked, False otherwise.
General ledger account number used to post retained earnings for this ledger during year-end closing. Represents accumulated profits or losses carried forward from prior periods.
Indicates whether this ledger tracks royalty payments and revenue related to licensed pharmaceutical intellectual property. True if royalty accounting is enabled, False otherwise.
Indicates whether this ledger is subject to Sarbanes-Oxley Act compliance requirements for internal controls over financial reporting. True if SOX-compliant controls are enforced, False otherwise.

Current operational status of the ledger. Active ledgers accept postings; inactive ledgers are temporarily disabled; closed ledgers are finalized for a fiscal period; suspended ledgers are under review; archived ledgers are retained for historical reference only.

Indicates whether this ledger supports profit and loss reporting segmented by therapeutic area (e.g., oncology, immunology, rare diseases). True if therapeutic area dimension is enabled, False otherwise.

Defines the valuation perspective for assets and liabilities in this ledger. Legal valuation follows statutory requirements; group valuation supports consolidation; profit center valuation enables segment reporting; tax valuation aligns with tax authority rules.
User identifier or system account that created this ledger record. Supports audit trail and accountability for ledger setup.

business_glossary_term: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Entry ID
description: Unique surrogate identifier for each COGS entry record in the silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for this data product.
reference: SAP CO-PC (Product Costing) internal record identifier

description: Reference to the specific manufacturing batch from which this COGS entry originates. Enables batch-level cost traceability and variance analysis per cGMP requirements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/QM Module; 21 CFR Parts 210/211; ICH Q7

description: Reference to the general ledger account to which this COGS entry is posted. Determines the financial statement line item classification for external and internal reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; US GAAP ASC 330; IFRS IAS 2; SOX Section 404

description: Reference to the CMO or CDMO vendor record when cmo_indicator is true. Enables COGS analysis by external manufacturing partner and supports vendor performance and cost benchmarking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Master; ICH Q10; GDP Guidelines

description: Reference to the SAP CO cost center responsible for incurring the manufacturing costs captured in this entry. Supports cost allocation and P&L reporting by organizational unit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; SOX Section 404

description: Identifier of the SAP CO-PC costing run that generated the standard cost estimate for this entry. Enables traceability of cost roll-up calculations and standard cost updates.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Module; ICH Q10

description: Reference to the finished drug product (DP) or finished dosage form (FDF) for which this COGS entry is recorded. Enables COGS analysis by product, brand, and therapeutic area.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master; ICH Q10 (Pharmaceutical Quality System)

description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: COGS entries post to GL accounts for financial reporting. The existing gl_account_code is a STRING; adding general_ledger_id FK establishes the relationship to the GL account master. This connects cog

Foreign key linking to supply.goods_issue. Business justification: Goods issues trigger COGS recognition in pharmaceutical accounting. Direct link required for inventory valuation, P&L accuracy, and audit trail from physical movement to financial posting. Standard ER

Foreign key linking to procurement.goods_receipt. Business justification: COGS postings triggered by goods receipts need direct linkage for inventory valuation and perpetual inventory accounting. Critical for FIFO/weighted average cost calculation, period-end inventory valu

Foreign key linking to supply.inventory_lot. Business justification: COGS recognition in pharma requires tracing to specific inventory lots for actual cost determination (FIFO/FEFO). Core inventory valuation and P&L process. New FK needed to link financial postings to

Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: COGS entries generate journal entries to record the cost of goods sold and inventory relief. The cogs_entry currently has sap_costing_doc_number (STRING) which should be replaced with a proper FK to j
Reference to the manufacturing plant or production facility where the drug product batch was produced. Supports COGS analysis by geography and manufacturing site.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP/MM Module; 21 CFR Parts 210/211 (cGMP)

description: Reference to the SAP CO profit center associated with this COGS entry. Enables P&L reporting by therapeutic area, brand, or business unit as required for management accounting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PCA Module; SOX Section 404

description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: COGS entries for purchased materials and CMO manufacturing services require PO traceability for cost reconciliation. Essential for standard cost vs. actual PO price variance analysis, transfer pricing

Reference to the specific SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) representing the packaged, market-ready form of the drug product. Enables COGS granularity at the sellable unit level for gross margin and pricing analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master; GS1 Standards

description: The actual cost incurred for the drug product batch or SKU as recorded in SAP CO-PC actual costing. Reflects real material consumption, labor hours, and overhead absorption during production.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Module; US GAAP ASC 330; IFRS IAS 2; SOX Section 404

description: The commercial brand name of the drug product associated with this COGS entry. Supports COGS and gross margin reporting at the brand level for commercial P&L analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master; FDA Drug Labeling; EMA Product Information

description: Flag indicating whether this COGS entry is eligible for R&D capitalization under applicable accounting standards (e.g., IFRS IAS 38 development phase costs). Supports the finance domain's R&D capitalization tracking process.
reference: IFRS IAS 38 (Intangible Assets); US GAAP ASC 730 (R&D Costs); SOX Section 404

description: Flag indicating whether this COGS entry relates to drug product manufactured by a Contract Manufacturing Organization (CMO) or Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) rather than internal manufacturing. Supports make-vs-buy cost analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Master; ICH Q10; 21 CFR Parts 210/211

description: Classification of the cost component captured in this COGS entry. Enables granular COGS decomposition into material (API/excipients), labor, overhead absorption, depreciation, and royalty components for margin analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: material|labor|overhead|depreciation|royalty|contract_manufacturing|quality_control|packaging|other — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Cost Component Structure; US GAAP ASC 330; IFRS IAS 2

description: The calculated cost per unit of drug product (standard or actual, per costing_type) derived from total cost divided by quantity produced. Used for pricing decisions, gross margin analysis, and transfer pricing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Unit Cost; US GAAP ASC 330; IFRS IAS 2

description: The difference between actual cost and standard cost (actual minus standard) for this COGS entry. Positive variance indicates cost overrun; negative indicates favorable performance. Critical for manufacturing efficiency analysis and pricing decisions.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Variance Analysis; US GAAP ASC 330; SOX Section 404

description: Classification of the costing methodology applied to this entry. Standard costing uses pre-set rates; actual costing uses real incurred costs. Determines how variances are calculated and reported.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Module; US GAAP ASC 330; IFRS IAS 2

description: Timestamp when this COGS entry record was first captured in the data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking per SOX compliance requirements.
reference: SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11; GDPR Article 5(2)

description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which all monetary amounts in this COGS entry are expressed (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). Supports multi-currency COGS reporting across global manufacturing sites.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA FI Currency Configuration; IFRS IAS 21

description: Current lifecycle status of the COGS entry within the financial posting workflow. Controls whether the entry is included in period-close reporting and gross margin calculations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO Module; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Section 302/404

description: The fiscal period (month 1–12 or 1–16 depending on fiscal year variant) within the fiscal year to which this COGS entry is attributed. Supports monthly gross margin reporting and period-close reconciliation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; US GAAP; IFRS; SOX Section 302

description: The fiscal year to which this COGS entry belongs, as defined in the SAP FI fiscal year variant. Used for annual P&L reporting, budget vs. actual comparisons, and SOX period-close controls.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; US GAAP; IFRS; SOX

description: The cost attributable to direct and indirect labor (production operators, QC analysts, supervisors) involved in manufacturing the batch. Sourced from SAP CO-PC labor cost component and PP work center confirmations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Labor Cost Component; PP Work Center; US GAAP ASC 330

description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the market/geography for which this COGS entry is recorded. Enables COGS analysis by geography to support regional P&L reporting and transfer pricing compliance.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; SAP S/4HANA SD Sales Organization; OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines

description: The cost attributable to raw materials, active pharmaceutical ingredients (API), excipients, and packaging materials consumed in producing the batch. Sourced from SAP CO-PC material cost component.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Material Cost Component; ICH Q7 (API GMP); US GAAP ASC 330

description: The FDA-assigned National Drug Code (NDC) for the drug product SKU. Enables linkage of COGS data to regulatory product registrations and commercial sales data for gross margin analysis.
reference: FDA NDC Directory; 21 CFR Part 207 (Drug Registration and Listing)

description: The manufacturing overhead costs (facility, utilities, equipment depreciation, indirect costs) absorbed into the product cost using overhead rates defined in SAP CO. Represents the overhead absorption component of COGS.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Overhead Cost Component; US GAAP ASC 330; IFRS IAS 2

description: The principal real-world financial event date on which the COGS entry was posted to the general ledger in SAP FI/CO. Determines the fiscal period to which the cost is attributed for P&L reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; IAS 2 (Inventories); US GAAP ASC 330

description: The quantity of drug product units (tablets, vials, doses, kg) produced in the manufacturing batch to which this COGS entry relates. Used to calculate per-unit cost and yield-adjusted COGS.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PP Production Order; 21 CFR Parts 210/211; ICH Q7

description: The unit of measure for the quantity produced field (e.g., EA for each, KG for kilograms, TAB for tablets, VIAL for vials). Aligns with SAP MM base unit of measure for the material. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|KG|L|MG|ML|TAB|VIAL|DOSE — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Unit of Measure; ISO 80000-1; GS1 Standards

description: The SAP FI document number of the reversal posting if this COGS entry has been reversed. Populated only when entry_status is 'reversed'. Supports audit trail and period-close reconciliation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Reversal Posting; SOX Section 404; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this COGS entry was sourced (e.g., SAP CO-PC for product costing, SAP PP for production orders, MES for manufacturing execution, or MANUAL for manual journal entries). Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX Section 404; ISPE GAMP 5

description: The pre-determined standard cost for the drug product batch or SKU as calculated by the SAP CO-PC costing run. Represents the expected cost under normal operating conditions and is the baseline for variance analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO-PC Module; US GAAP ASC 330; IFRS IAS 2; SOX Section 404

description: The therapeutic area classification of the drug product (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Enables P&L and COGS analysis by therapeutic area as required for management reporting and R&D investment decisions. reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312/314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; MHRA; PMDA; NMPA; ICH M4

description: Name of the party (licensor, licensee, or co-development partner) contractually responsible for achieving the milestone trigger event or making the milestone payment. Supports partner relationship management and deal accountability tracking.
reference: Veeva Vault RIM; SAP S/4HANA SD Contract Management

description: Indicates whether the milestone payment has been recognized as revenue in the financial statements under ASC 606 / IFRS 15. True = revenue recognized; False = not yet recognized or deferred. Supports finance and SOX compliance reporting.
reference: ASC 606; IFRS 15; SOX Section 302/404; SAP S/4HANA FI Revenue Accounting

description: Annual or cumulative net sales threshold that must be reached to trigger a commercial sales-based milestone payment, expressed in the agreement currency. Applicable only to commercial milestone types with net sales triggers.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD/FI; ASC 606; IFRS 15; SOX Section 302/404

description: SAP S/4HANA FI invoice or billing document number generated upon milestone achievement and payment invoicing. Enables reconciliation between the IP milestone record and the financial accounting system.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Accounts Receivable/Payable; SOX Section 302/404

description: Ordinal sequence number of this milestone within the agreement, as defined in the agreement schedule (e.g., 1 = first milestone, 2 = second milestone). Supports ordered reporting and deal progress tracking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Contract Management; Veeva Vault RIM

description: Type of regulatory submission associated with a regulatory milestone trigger event. Applicable when milestone_type is 'regulatory'. Values: IND (Investigational New Drug), NDA (New Drug Application), BLA (Biologics License Application), MAA (Marketing Authorization Application), sNDA (supplemental NDA), sBLA (supplemental BLA), or other. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IND|NDA|BLA|MAA|sNDA|sBLA|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH M4 eCTD

description: Geographic territory or jurisdiction in which the milestone trigger event must occur for the milestone to be payable (e.g., USA, EU, JPN, Worldwide). Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes or named multi-country regions as defined in the agreement.
reference: ISO 3166-1; SAP S/4HANA SD; Veeva Vault RIM

description: Therapeutic area or disease indication to which the licensed product and this milestone apply (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience). Supports portfolio analytics and deal management reporting.
reference: ATC Classification System; WHO ICD-11; Internal Therapeutic Area Taxonomy

description: Specific contractual event or condition that triggers this milestone obligation, as defined in the agreement (e.g., 'Receipt of written FDA approval of NDA for Product X in the United States', 'First patient dosed in Phase I clinical trial'). Supports legal review and milestone verification.
reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Licensing Agreements

description: Timestamp when this milestone record was last modified in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and change tracking requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX.

Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM or QualityDocs referencing the agreement schedule, milestone amendment, or supporting evidence document for this milestone. Enables traceability to the source controlled document.
reference: Veeva Vault RIM; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Electronic Records Guidance

description: Amount of withholding tax deducted from the milestone payment, as applicable under the governing tax treaty between the licensor and licensee jurisdictions. Recorded in SAP FI for tax compliance reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Tax Management; OECD Model Tax Convention; IFRS 12

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the licensing agreement record in the intellectual property portfolio system.

business_glossary_term: Internal Deal Owner Employee Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical business development requires employee ownership of licensing agreements for milestone tracking, diligence monitoring, and contract administration. Replaces text field internal_deal_own

Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: Licensing agreements require tracking licensor legal entity for contract management, revenue recognition, and intercompany royalty accounting in pharmaceutical partnerships.

Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: In-licensing agreements often involve API/technology suppliers as licensors. Linking enables supplier qualification, audit tracking, and contract management integration. Licensor_name is denormalized;

Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: License agreements generate costs/revenues allocated to cost centers; required for P&L reporting, royalty expense tracking, and business unit accountability.

Foreign key linking to masterdata.profit_center. Business justification: License agreements are assigned to business segments; required for revenue recognition, segment P&L reporting, and royalty income allocation.

Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_program. Business justification: Licensing agreements are governed by compliance programs (anti-bribery, transfer pricing, IP compliance, conflict of interest). Program oversight ensures regulatory adherence and third-party due dilig

Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: License territories define geographic scope; essential for revenue allocation, royalty calculation, and compliance with territorial restrictions in pharmaceutical licensing.

Externally-known, human-readable reference number assigned to the licensing agreement, used in correspondence with counterparties, legal counsel, and regulatory filings. Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER for this MASTER_AGREEMENT entity.

Current lifecycle state of the licensing agreement. Draft: under negotiation. Active: fully executed and in force. Suspended: temporarily paused by mutual consent or breach notice. Terminated: ended before natural expiry. Expired: reached end of term without renewal. Drives deal management workflows and financial reporting.

Classification of the licensing agreement by deal structure. In-licensing: rights acquired from a third party. Out-licensing: rights granted to a third party. Cross-licensing: mutual exchange of IP rights. Co-development: joint development with shared IP. Collaboration: broad research or commercialization partnership. Drives revenue recognition treatment under ASC 606.

Indicates whether the agreement contains a change-of-control clause that grants termination or renegotiation rights upon acquisition or merger of either party. True = change-of-control provision exists; False = no such provision. Critical for M&A due diligence and IP portfolio valuation.
reference: SOX Section 302; SEC Regulation S-K; ICH Q10

description: Aggregate value of all commercial milestone payments (e.g., first commercial sale, annual net sales thresholds) defined in the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Supports commercial launch planning and ASC 606 variable consideration estimation.

Timestamp when the licensing agreement record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED audit trail required for 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and SOX financial reporting controls.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which all financial obligations under the agreement (upfront payments, milestones, royalties) are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY, GBP). Required for multi-currency royalty accounting and foreign exchange hedging.

Aggregate value of all development-stage milestone payments (e.g., IND submission, Phase I/II/III completion) defined in the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Supports clinical development budget planning and ASC 606 variable consideration estimation.
reference: ASC 606; IFRS 15; 21 CFR Part 312; ICH E6(R2)

description: Narrative description of the commercially reasonable efforts or best efforts diligence obligations imposed on the licensee to develop and commercialize the licensed product. Failure to meet diligence obligations may trigger termination rights. Used for partner relationship management and compliance monitoring.

Contractually agreed mechanism for resolving disputes between the parties. Arbitration: binding arbitration under specified rules (e.g., ICC, AAA). Litigation: resolution through courts of the governing jurisdiction. Mediation: non-binding mediation before escalation. Expert-determination: technical disputes resolved by independent expert.
reference: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 314; SOX Section 302

description: Date on which the licensing agreement becomes legally binding and operative. Marks the start of the agreement term for royalty accrual, exclusivity period calculation, and milestone tracking. Corresponds to EFFECTIVE_FROM for the MASTER_AGREEMENT role.

Scope of exclusivity granted under the license. Exclusive: licensee is the sole permitted user in the territory/field. Non-exclusive: licensor may grant same rights to others. Co-exclusive: limited number of licensees permitted. Semi-exclusive: licensor retains right to practice but not to license others. Critical for generic/biosimilar entry defense strategy.
reference: USPTO Patent Rules; 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10

description: Date on which the licensing agreement was formally signed and executed by all parties. May differ from the effective date if the agreement has a retroactive or future effective date. Used for legal record-keeping and audit trails.

Date on which the licensing agreement naturally expires at the end of its agreed term. Nullable for perpetual or open-ended agreements. Drives lifecycle management alerts, renewal negotiations, and IP exclusivity planning. Corresponds to EFFECTIVE_UNTIL for the MASTER_AGREEMENT role.

Specific therapeutic area, indication, or application domain within which the licensee is permitted to use the licensed IP. Examples: 'oncology', 'rare diseases', 'human therapeutics only', 'diagnostic use'. Restricts the scope of the license and is critical for exclusivity analysis and sublicensing rights management.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314; ICH E6(R2); USPTO Patent Rules

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction whose laws govern the interpretation and enforcement of the agreement. Determines applicable contract law, dispute resolution procedures, and regulatory compliance obligations.

Timestamp when the licensing agreement record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED audit trail required for 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and change control tracking.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5

description: Name or identifier of the internal or external legal counsel responsible for drafting, negotiating, and maintaining the agreement. Used for coordination on patent litigation, IP enforcement, and contract amendments.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314; USPTO Patent Rules; SOX Section 302

description: Narrative description of the intellectual property assets covered by the license, including compound names (INN/USAN), patent numbers, know-how, trade secrets, trademarks, or biological sequences. Supports IP portfolio management and freedom-to-operate analysis.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10; USPTO Patent Rules

description: Classification of the primary intellectual property asset type covered by the agreement. Patent: granted patent rights. Know-how: proprietary technical knowledge. Trademark: brand or trade name rights. Data-package: regulatory data exclusivity or clinical data. Biological-sequence: gene or protein sequence rights. Trade-secret: confidential proprietary information. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: patent|know-how|trademark|data-package|biological-sequence|trade-secret|formulation|process — promote to reference product]
reference: USPTO Patent Rules; 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10

description: Full legal name of the party receiving the license (the licensee). For in-licensing agreements, this is typically the company itself. For out-licensing, this is the external counterparty receiving rights. Used in legal documentation, royalty accounting, and partner relationship management.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10; GDPR Article 4

description: Total number of contractually defined milestone events (development, regulatory, and commercial) specified in the agreement. Used for milestone tracking dashboards, deal management reporting, and ASC 606 performance obligation identification.

Aggregate value of all regulatory milestone payments (e.g., NDA/BLA/MAA submission, FDA/EMA approval) defined in the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Supports regulatory affairs planning and ASC 606 variable consideration estimation.
reference: ASC 606; IFRS 15; 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004

description: Identifies which party bears primary responsibility for conducting development activities (clinical trials, regulatory submissions, manufacturing scale-up) under the agreement. Licensor: licensor retains development responsibility. Licensee: licensee assumes development responsibility. Joint: shared responsibility as defined in the agreement.

Indicates whether the agreement grants either party a right of first negotiation (ROFN) for additional territories, indications, or follow-on compounds. True = ROFN exists; False = no ROFN. Relevant for lifecycle management and business development strategy.
reference: USPTO Patent Rules; ICH Q10; SOX Section 302

description: The contractual basis on which royalties are calculated. Net-sales: royalties applied to net sales after standard deductions. Gross-sales: royalties applied to gross sales before deductions. Net-revenue: royalties applied to net revenue. Units-sold: royalties calculated per unit sold. Determines the royalty accounting methodology.

Contractual royalty rate expressed as a decimal fraction of net sales (e.g., 0.050000 = 5.0%) payable by the licensee to the licensor. Used for royalty accrual calculations, revenue recognition under ASC 606/IFRS 15, and P&L forecasting. Null if the agreement uses a tiered royalty structure captured in a separate milestone/royalty schedule.

Contract number assigned in SAP S/4HANA (SD or FI module) for financial processing of royalty payments, milestone invoicing, and upfront fee recognition. Enables reconciliation between the IP portfolio system and the ERP for royalty accounting and revenue recognition.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD/FI; ASC 606; SOX Section 302

description: Indicates whether the licensee has the contractual right to sublicense the licensed IP to third parties (e.g., CMOs, CDMOs, or sub-distributors). True = sublicensing permitted; False = sublicensing prohibited. Impacts CMO/CDMO engagement and supply chain structuring.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314; ICH Q10; USPTO Patent Rules

description: Summary of the contractual conditions under which either party may terminate the agreement, including material breach cure periods, insolvency triggers, regulatory failure events, and convenience termination rights. Used by legal counsel for contract management and risk assessment.
reference: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 314; SOX Section 302

description: Date on which the licensing agreement was terminated prior to its natural expiry, whether by mutual consent, breach, or exercise of termination rights. Null if the agreement has not been terminated. Used for financial close-out and IP rights reversion tracking.

Total potential deal value including upfront payments, all milestone payments, and estimated royalties over the agreement term, expressed in the agreement currency. Used for deal valuation, P&L forecasting, and investor disclosure. Represents the gross deal value before probability-weighting.
reference: ASC 606; IFRS 15; SOX Section 302; SEC Regulation S-K

description: Sum of all contractually defined milestone payment amounts across all milestone events in the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Represents the maximum milestone-based consideration achievable under the agreement. Used for deal valuation and revenue recognition planning.

One-time upfront license fee or signing payment due at execution of the agreement, expressed in the agreement currency. Recognized as revenue or capitalized as an intangible asset depending on the nature of the license under ASC 606/IFRS 15. Part of the MONETARY_TRIPLET for this MASTER_AGREEMENT.

Reference identifier of the fully executed agreement document stored in Veeva Vault (RIM or QualityDocs module). Enables direct navigation from the data product record to the source legal document for audit, due diligence, and regulatory inspection purposes. Aligns with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault RIM; SOX Section 302

description: Unique system-generated identifier for each royalty payment transaction record within the intellectual property portfolio management system.

Foreign key linking to finance.journal_entry. Business justification: Every royalty payment (in or out) generates a GL posting for revenue/expense recognition. Finance links royalty payments to journal entries for reconciliation, audit trail, SOX compliance, and revenue
Reference to the licensing agreement under which this royalty payment is made or received. Links the payment to the governing contract terms.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; ICH Q10

description: Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Royalty payments calculated on product-specific net sales. Essential for financial reporting, deal reconciliation, and product-level P&L attribution. Removes denormalized licensed_product_name.
Reference to the patent or intellectual property asset (NCE, NBE, formulation, or process patent) that is the subject of the royalty-bearing license.
Reference to the party granting the license (the entity receiving royalty payments in an outbound scenario or paying in an inbound scenario).

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical finance assigns employees to reconcile royalty payments for calculation validation, dispute resolution, and treasury coordination. Critical for revenue recognition, audit trail, and SOX

Any adjustments applied to the calculated royalty amount, such as corrections from prior period reconciliations, audit findings, or contractual true-ups. Positive values increase the payment; negative values reduce it.
reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX

description: Indicates whether this royalty payment record has been flagged for formal royalty audit review, typically triggered by discrepancies between reported sales and expected royalty amounts or by contractual audit rights.
Bank-issued transaction reference number or wire transfer confirmation number associated with the royalty payment. Used for bank reconciliation and payment verification.

End date of the royalty calculation period for which net sales or units sold are being reported and royalties computed. Together with start date defines the reporting window per the licensing agreement.

Start date of the royalty calculation period (e.g., quarter or year) for which net sales or units sold are being reported and royalties computed. Aligns with licensing agreement reporting obligations.
SAP cost center code to which the royalty payment expense or income is allocated for internal management accounting and P&L reporting purposes.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; GAAP/IFRS; SOX

description: Timestamp when this royalty payment record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under SOX and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
reference: SOX; 21 CFR Part 11; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the royalty payment transaction (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). Determines the denomination of all monetary amounts in this record.
reference: ISO 4217; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; GAAP/IFRS

description: Total allowable deductions applied to gross sales to arrive at net sales, as defined in the licensing agreement. Typically includes chargebacks, rebates, returns, freight, and applicable taxes.
reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; SOX

description: Free-text description of the reason for disputing the royalty payment amount, applicable when payment_status is 'disputed'. Documents the basis for disagreement between licensor and licensee for legal and audit purposes.
Contractual deadline by which the royalty payment must be made as specified in the licensing agreement. Used to track overdue payments and trigger escalation workflows.

Foreign exchange rate applied to convert the transaction currency to the company's functional reporting currency at the time of payment. Required for multi-currency licensing agreements and consolidated financial reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; GAAP/IFRS IAS 21

description: Total payment amount converted to the company's functional reporting currency using the applicable exchange rate. Used for consolidated P&L reporting and SOX financial controls.
reference: GAAP/IFRS IAS 21; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX

description: SAP General Ledger account code to which this royalty payment is posted for financial reporting purposes. Distinguishes royalty income (inbound) from royalty expense (outbound) in the P&L.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO Module; GAAP/IFRS; SOX

description: Total gross sales revenue generated from the licensed product during the calculation period, before any deductions. Used as the starting point for net sales calculation per the licensing agreement definition.
reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; SOX

description: Geographic territory or market for which the royalty payment applies, as defined in the licensing agreement. May be a country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3), region, or 'GLOBAL'. Supports territory-level royalty analytics.
reference: ISO 3166-1; Licensing Agreement Terms; FDA; EMA

description: Contractual minimum royalty amount guaranteed per period as specified in the licensing agreement, regardless of actual sales performance. Applicable when the calculated royalty falls below this floor.

Net sales revenue for the licensed product during the calculation period, calculated as gross sales minus allowable deductions per the licensing agreement definition. Forms the royalty basis for net-sales-based agreements.
reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA SD Module; SOX

description: The actual date on which the royalty payment was executed (funds transferred or received). Represents the principal real-world business event date for this transaction.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX; GAAP/IFRS

description: Indicates whether the royalty payment is inbound (received by the company as licensor) or outbound (paid by the company as licensee). Critical for P&L classification and financial reporting.
The financial instrument or mechanism used to execute the royalty payment (e.g., wire transfer, ACH, check, offset against receivables, or netting against other obligations).
Externally-known business identifier for this royalty payment transaction, typically matching the SAP FI document number or bank remittance reference used for reconciliation and audit trail.

Current lifecycle state of the royalty payment transaction. Tracks progression from draft calculation through approval, payment execution, and final settlement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending|approved|paid|disputed|cancelled — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]

Current status of the royalty payment reconciliation process, indicating whether the payment has been matched against the licensee's royalty report and confirmed as accurate. Supports royalty audit workflows.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX; GAAP/IFRS

description: Calculated royalty amount due for the calculation period, derived by applying the royalty rate to the applicable royalty basis (net sales, gross sales, or units sold). This is the principal monetary fact of the transaction.
reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX

description: The contractual basis upon which the royalty is calculated, as defined in the licensing agreement. Common bases include net sales, gross sales, units sold, milestone achievements, or sublicense revenue.

The contractual royalty rate applied to the royalty basis (expressed as a decimal fraction, e.g., 0.05 for 5%). May be tiered based on sales thresholds as defined in the licensing agreement. Classified confidential as it reflects proprietary deal terms.

Reference number or identifier of the royalty statement or sales report submitted by the licensee that forms the basis for this royalty payment calculation. Links the payment to the supporting documentation.

Label identifying the applicable royalty tier when the licensing agreement specifies tiered rates based on cumulative net sales thresholds (e.g., 'Tier 1: 0-$100M', 'Tier 2: $100M-$500M'). Null if the agreement uses a flat rate.
Therapeutic area classification of the licensed drug product (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases). Supports portfolio-level royalty analytics and strategic lifecycle management decisions.
Final net royalty payment amount after applying the royalty rate to the basis, enforcing any minimum royalty floor, and incorporating adjustments. This is the amount actually paid or received.
reference: GAAP/IFRS; SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX

description: Number of units of the licensed product sold during the calculation period. Used as the royalty basis for unit-based royalty agreements. Expressed as DECIMAL to accommodate partial units or volume-based measures.
reference: Licensing Agreement Terms; SAP S/4HANA SD Module

description: Timestamp when this royalty payment record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and data lineage in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOX; 21 CFR Part 11; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

description: Amount of withholding tax deducted from the royalty payment at source, as required by applicable tax treaties between the licensor and licensee jurisdictions. Relevant for cross-border licensing arrangements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; OECD Tax Treaties; GAAP/IFRS

description: Applicable withholding tax rate (expressed as a decimal fraction) applied to the royalty payment based on the tax treaty between the relevant jurisdictions. Used to validate withholding tax amount calculations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; OECD Tax Treaties

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each patent annuity (maintenance fee) payment obligation or payment record in the portfolio.

Foreign key linking to finance.accounts_payable. Business justification: Patent annuity fees are paid to patent offices via accounts payable. Finance links annuity fee records to AP invoices for payment tracking, accrual reconciliation, cost center allocation, and annual I

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical IP operations require employee authorization for annuity payments for budget control, lapse prevention, and SOX compliance. Replaces text field authorized_by with employee FK for audit
Reference to the patent record in the intellectual property portfolio for which this annuity fee obligation applies.

The bank transaction reference number or wire transfer confirmation number associated with the annuity fee payment, used for financial reconciliation against the company's bank statements and SAP FI records.
reference: SOX; IFRS IAS 21; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

description: Official receipt or acknowledgement number issued by the patent office or paying agent confirming successful payment of the annuity fee. Serves as proof of payment for audit and compliance purposes.
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.8; EPO Rule 51 EPC; 21 CFR Part 11; SOX

description: The SAP S/4HANA cost center code to which the annuity fee expense is allocated, enabling departmental cost tracking and IP portfolio cost management reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Module; SOX; Internal Finance Policy

description: The commercial or INN (International Nonproprietary Name) of the pharmaceutical product covered by the patent for which this annuity fee is being maintained. Supports commercial impact analysis and lifecycle management decisions.
reference: INN (International Nonproprietary Name); WHO INN Programme; ICH Q10

description: The date and time when this annuity fee record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Used for audit trail and data lineage compliance.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; SOX; GDPR Article 5; ISO 8601

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the jurisdiction in which the annuity fee is payable (e.g., USD for US dollars, EUR for euros, JPY for Japanese yen, GBP for British pounds).
The statutory deadline by which the annuity fee must be paid to maintain the patent in force in the relevant jurisdiction. Missing this date without a grace period payment results in patent lapse.
reference: USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPO Rule 51 EPC; PCT Rule 22bis; MHRA; PMDA

description: The entity size classification applicable to this annuity fee payment, which determines the applicable fee discount at the USPTO and certain other patent offices. Large entities pay full fees; small entities (fewer than 500 employees) pay 60% of large entity fees; micro entities pay 40% of large entity fees.

The foreign exchange rate applied to convert the local jurisdiction currency amount to the company's functional reporting currency at the time of payment. Used for financial consolidation and cost tracking.
The official annuity fee amount due to the patent office in the local jurisdiction currency, as prescribed by the applicable fee schedule for the relevant fee year and entity size category.
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.20; EPO Rule 51 EPC; ISO 4217

description: Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this annuity fee obligation, typically generated by the paying agent or internal IP management system for tracking and reconciliation purposes.
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.20; EPO Rule 51 EPC; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The version or effective date of the patent office fee schedule used to determine the annuity fee amount for this payment obligation. Fee schedules are periodically updated by patent offices and the applicable version must be documented for audit purposes.
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.20; EPO Rule 51 EPC; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The renewal year number for which the annuity fee is due, counting from the patent filing or grant date depending on jurisdiction rules (e.g., year 3, year 10, year 20). Critical for determining the applicable fee schedule.
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.20; EPO Rule 51 EPC; PCT Rule 22bis

description: The total annuity payment amount converted to the company's functional reporting currency (typically USD or EUR) using the applicable exchange rate. Used for financial reporting, budget tracking, and IP cost management.

The SAP S/4HANA General Ledger account code to which the annuity fee expense is posted for financial reporting and cost tracking purposes. Enables integration between IP management and financial accounting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI Module; SOX; IFRS IAS 38

description: The final date by which a late annuity fee payment can be made with a surcharge to avoid patent lapse, as permitted by the relevant patent office. Varies by jurisdiction (e.g., 6 months in the US, typically with surcharge).
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.137; EPO Rule 51(2) EPC; PCT Rule 22bis

description: The date on which the internal instruction or authorization to pay the annuity fee was issued to the paying agent or treasury function. Represents the business event timestamp when the payment process was initiated.
reference: SOX; 21 CFR Part 11; Internal IP Management Policy

description: The country or regional patent authority jurisdiction in which the annuity fee is payable, expressed as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code (e.g., USA, GBR, DEU, JPN, CHN) or regional office code (e.g., EPO for European Patent Office).
reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; WIPO; USPTO; EPO; PMDA; NMPA; MHRA

description: The date on which the patent lapsed in the jurisdiction due to non-payment of the annuity fee. Populated only when payment_status is 'lapsed'. Critical for tracking portfolio attrition and generic/biosimilar entry risk.
reference: USPTO 35 U.S.C. § 41; EPO Rule 51 EPC; Internal IP Portfolio Management Policy

description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, special instructions, dispute details, or operational notes related to this annuity fee record, such as correspondence with the patent office or paying agent.
reference: Internal IP Management Policy; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Name of the external annuity service provider or patent renewal agent (e.g., CPA Global, Dennemeyer, Questel, Anaqua) engaged to manage and remit annuity fee payments on behalf of the company in the relevant jurisdiction.
reference: USPTO; EPO; WIPO; Internal IP Management Policy

description: The unique reference or docket number assigned by the external paying agent to this annuity fee instruction, used for reconciliation and correspondence with the agent.
reference: Internal IP Management Policy; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The actual date on which the annuity fee payment was remitted to the patent office or paying agent. Null if payment has not yet been made.
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.20; EPO Rule 51 EPC; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The financial instrument or mechanism used to remit the annuity fee payment to the patent office or paying agent (e.g., bank transfer, USPTO deposit account, credit card, electronic funds transfer).
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.23; EPO Rule 51 EPC; PCI DSS

description: Current lifecycle status of the annuity fee payment obligation. 'paid' indicates the fee has been successfully remitted; 'overdue' indicates the due date has passed without payment; 'waived' indicates the fee has been formally waived (e.g., small entity, micro-entity); 'lapsed' indicates the patent has lapsed due to non-payment; 'pending' indicates payment is in process; 'scheduled' indicates payment is queued for future processing.
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.137; EPO Rule 51 EPC; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Indicates whether the lapsed patent is eligible for reinstatement or restoration under the applicable jurisdiction's rules (e.g., USPTO petition for revival, EPO re-establishment of rights). Relevant only when payment_status is 'lapsed'.
reference: USPTO 37 CFR Part 1.137; EPO Rule 136 EPC

description: The date on which the annuity fee payment reminder was dispatched to the responsible party. Null if no reminder has been sent. Used to track notification compliance and escalation timelines.

Indicates whether an automated or manual payment reminder notification has been sent to the responsible IP manager or paying agent ahead of the annuity fee due date. Supports proactive portfolio maintenance workflows.
reference: Internal IP Management Policy; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The SAP S/4HANA FI payment document number generated when the annuity fee payment is posted in the financial system, enabling end-to-end reconciliation between IP management records and the general ledger.
