Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: IP watch records track competitive intelligence on third-party patents that may threaten the company's freedom to operate. The patent_number (STRING) should be replaced with a FK to patent.patent_id t

Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_risk_register. Business justification: IP watch activities (competitor filings, Paragraph IV notices, biosimilar applications) identify compliance risks (exclusivity loss, revenue at risk, litigation exposure) that populate risk registers

The National Drug Code (NDC) of the specific drug product formulation or SKU threatened by the competitor's filing. Enables precise linkage to the commercial product portfolio and Orange Book listings.

The proprietary or International Nonproprietary Name (INN) of the company's drug product that is potentially threatened by the competitor's IP activity. Supports linkage to commercial and lifecycle management decisions.
reference: WHO INN Programme; FDA Orange Book; Internal Product Master

description: The name of the regulatory or intellectual property authority with which the competitor's filing was made, such as FDA, EMA, USPTO, EPO, PMDA, or NMPA. Provides context for applicable rules and timelines.
reference: FDA; EMA; USPTO; EPO; PMDA; NMPA; ICH

description: Indicates whether the competitor's aBLA biosimilar application seeks an interchangeability designation with the company's reference biologic product. Interchangeable biosimilars may be substituted at the pharmacy level without prescriber intervention, representing a higher commercial threat.
reference: 42 U.S.C. § 262(k)(4); FDA Biosimilar Interchangeability Guidance; BPCIA (Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act)

description: The date on which the IP watch record was formally closed, indicating that the threat has been resolved, the litigation concluded, the competitor's application was withdrawn or rejected, or the matter is no longer actively monitored.

Estimated annual revenue (in USD) of the affected product that is at risk of erosion if the competitor's generic or biosimilar entry is successful. Used to prioritize IP defense investment and inform lifecycle management decisions.
reference: Internal Commercial Finance Policy; SOX Financial Reporting Compliance

description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country of incorporation or principal operations of the competitor entity filing the IP activity.
Name of the third-party company or entity that filed the competing patent, ANDA, aBLA, or patent challenge being monitored. Critical for competitive intelligence and IP defense strategy.

The timestamp at which this IP watch record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); Internal Data Governance Policy

description: The date on which the company's IP watch function first identified or was notified of the competitor's filing or IP activity. Used to measure response time and early warning effectiveness.

business_glossary_term: Estimated Generic or Biosimilar Market Entry Date
description: The estimated date on which the competitor's generic drug or biosimilar product could enter the market, based on patent expiry, exclusivity expiry, regulatory approval timelines, and litigation outcomes. Critical for lifecycle management and revenue forecasting.
reference: FDA Orange Book; FDA Biosimilar Product Information; Internal Lifecycle Management Framework

description: The type of regulatory exclusivity period that may be threatened or circumvented by the competitor's filing, such as orphan drug exclusivity, data exclusivity, pediatric exclusivity, New Chemical Entity (NCE) exclusivity, New Biological Entity (NBE) exclusivity, or Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) protection.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314.108 (NCE Exclusivity); Orphan Drug Act; BPCIA; Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Exclusivity Database

description: The date on which the competitor filed the patent application, ANDA, aBLA, or patent challenge with the relevant regulatory or IP authority. This is the principal real-world event date for the watch record.
reference: USPTO Filing Rules; 21 CFR Part 314.94; EMA Biosimilar Guidelines

description: The official reference number assigned by the regulatory or IP authority to the competitor's filing, such as an ANDA application number, aBLA application number, USPTO patent application number, or IPR petition number. Enables direct cross-referencing with public databases.
reference: FDA ANDA Database; USPTO Patent Center; EMA Biosimilar Register

description: Indicates whether a Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis is required in response to the competitor's patent filing or IP activity, to assess whether the company's products or processes may infringe the competitor's claims.
reference: Internal IP Due Diligence SOP; USPTO Patent Examination Guidelines

description: Current status of the Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis associated with this IP watch record, tracking whether the analysis has been initiated, is in progress, or has been completed.

Indicates whether the company has filed a patent infringement lawsuit in response to the competitor's Paragraph IV certification or other IP challenge. Triggers the 30-month stay of FDA approval under Hatch-Waxman.
The date on which the company filed the patent infringement lawsuit in response to the IP threat. Must be within 45 days of receiving the Paragraph IV notice letter to trigger the 30-month stay.
Name of the external law firm engaged to represent the company in litigation or IP proceedings related to this watch record. Classified as confidential due to legal strategy sensitivity.
reference: Internal Legal Engagement Policy; Attorney-Client Privilege Guidelines

description: Indicates whether the competitor's ANDA or 505(b)(2) submission includes a Paragraph IV certification asserting that the company's listed patent is invalid or will not be infringed. Triggers the 30-month stay provision under the Hatch-Waxman Act.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314.94(a)(12)(i)(A)(4); Hatch-Waxman Act (Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act)

business_glossary_term: Paragraph IV Notice Letter Receipt Date
description: The date on which the company received the formal Paragraph IV notice letter from the ANDA or 505(b)(2) applicant, as required under the Hatch-Waxman Act. The 45-day window to file suit and trigger the 30-month stay begins from this date.

The recommended strategic or legal response to the identified IP threat, such as filing a patent infringement lawsuit, filing an IPR petition, seeking a preliminary injunction, entering licensing negotiations, or monitoring without action. Classified as confidential due to legal strategy sensitivity.
reference: Internal IP Defense Strategy SOP; USPTO IPR Rules (37 CFR Part 42)

description: The final outcome of the IP dispute or watch activity upon closure, indicating whether the matter was settled (e.g., licensing agreement), won by the company, lost (competitor entry permitted), withdrawn by the competitor, dismissed by the authority, or remains ongoing.
reference: Internal IP Litigation Tracking SOP; USPTO Trial and Appeal Board Rules

description: The statutory or internally-set deadline by which the company must initiate a legal or regulatory response to the IP threat (e.g., 45-day deadline to file suit following Paragraph IV notice, IPR petition deadline of 1 year from service of infringement complaint).
reference: 21 CFR Part 314.107; 35 U.S.C. § 315(b) (IPR Petition Deadline); Hatch-Waxman Act

description: Narrative summary of the risk assessment conducted by the IP and legal team, describing the basis for the risk level assignment, key vulnerabilities, and potential commercial exposure. Classified as confidential due to legal strategy sensitivity.
reference: Internal IP Risk Assessment SOP; Attorney-Client Privilege Guidelines

description: Assessed risk level of the IP threat to the company's portfolio, reflecting the likelihood of successful generic or biosimilar entry and the commercial impact. Drives prioritization of legal and IP defense resources.
reference: Internal IP Risk Assessment Framework; ICH Q9 (Quality Risk Management)

description: The scientific or technical domain of the IP activity, such as small molecule chemistry, biologics, formulation technology, manufacturing process, delivery device, or specific therapeutic mechanism. Aligns with internal R&D and IP portfolio taxonomy.
reference: ICH Q8 (Pharmaceutical Development); ICH Q11 (Development and Manufacture of Drug Substances)

description: The disease or clinical indication area relevant to the IP activity, such as oncology, immunology, rare diseases, cardiovascular, or neurology. Used to prioritize IP defense resources by commercial importance.
reference: WHO ATC Classification; Internal Therapeutic Area Taxonomy

description: The date on which the 30-month stay of FDA approval expires following a Paragraph IV certification and timely patent infringement lawsuit. Null if no Paragraph IV certification was filed. Critical for generic entry timeline planning.
The timestamp at which this IP watch record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records and Signatures); Internal Data Governance Policy

description: Free-text field for additional context, observations, or legal strategy notes related to the IP watch record, entered by the IP analyst or legal counsel. Classified as confidential due to potential legal strategy content.

Externally-known business identifier assigned to this IP watch record, used for cross-referencing with legal counsel, RIMS, and Veeva Vault RIM module. Typically follows a structured format such as IPW-YYYY-NNNNNN.
reference: Veeva Vault RIM; Internal IP Management SOP

description: The source or monitoring service through which the IP activity was identified, such as FDA Orange Book, FDA ANDA database, USPTO patent database, EPO database, EMA biosimilar register, Derwent Innovation, Clarivate IP watch service, or internal monitoring. reference: FDA Orange Book; USPTO Patent Center; EPO Espacenet; EMA Biosimilar Register

description: Current lifecycle state of the IP watch record, indicating whether the threat is newly identified (open), being assessed (under_review), escalated to legal or senior management, actively monitored (monitoring), or resolved (closed).

Classification of the third-party IP activity being monitored. Covers competitor patent filings, Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) submissions, 505(b)(2) submissions, abbreviated Biologics License Application (aBLA) biosimilar filings, patent challenges (e.g., IPR, PGR, inter partes review), and trademark oppositions.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314 (ANDA); 21 CFR Part 351 (aBLA); USPTO Inter Partes Review Rules; FDA Orange Book

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each patent litigation case record in the intellectual property portfolio management system.

Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Litigation occurs in specific jurisdictions; required for legal strategy, financial reserves estimation, and paragraph IV defense planning in pharmaceutical patent disputes.

Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: ANDA Paragraph IV litigation tracks generic manufacturers (vendors) as defendants. Linking enables risk assessment for vendor qualification, supply continuity planning, and commercial impact analysis.

Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_incident. Business justification: Patent litigation should link to compliance incidents for IP disputes that constitute compliance or legal risk events. This enables integrated risk management across IP and compliance domains.

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical patent litigation requires internal counsel ownership for case strategy, budget management, and outside counsel coordination. Replaces text field internal_counsel_name with employee FK

Foreign key linking to intellectual.ip_watch. Business justification: IP watch records track competitive threats (e.g., Paragraph IV ANDA filings, competitor patent applications). When a watch escalates to actual litigation, the patent_litigation record should link back

Foreign key linking to masterdata.cost_center. Business justification: Litigation costs are allocated to business units; essential for legal spend tracking, forecasting, and financial impact assessment of patent disputes.

Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: Patent litigation targets specific products (Paragraph IV, biosimilar challenges). Essential for commercial risk assessment, legal spend tracking, revenue-at-risk forecasting. Removes denormalized pro

Foreign key linking to intellectual.orange_book_listing. Business justification: Patent litigation in pharmaceuticals is often triggered by Paragraph IV certifications challenging Orange Book-listed patents. Linking patent_litigation to orange_book_listing tracks which Orange Book

Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_inspection. Business justification: Patent litigation (Paragraph IV ANDA challenges, biosimilar disputes) can trigger regulatory inspections. Inspection outcomes affect litigation strategy and settlement negotiations. Essential for coor

Foreign key linking to compliance.warning_letter. Business justification: Patent litigation related to data integrity violations or GXP non-compliance can result in warning letters. Litigation discovery may reveal compliance failures requiring coordinated legal and quality

Cumulative actual legal fees and costs incurred to date for this litigation matter, expressed in US dollars. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA FI/CO module legal spend tracking. Used for legal budget management and P&L reporting.
reference: ASC 450; SOX Section 302; SAP S/4HANA FI Module

description: Name of the appellate court or tribunal hearing the appeal (e.g., U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, U.S. Supreme Court, EPO Board of Appeal). Null if no appeal has been filed.
reference: 35 U.S.C. § 141; Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure

description: Indicates whether an appeal has been filed following the trial court or PTAB judgment. True if an appeal is pending or has been decided; False if no appeal was filed.
reference: 35 U.S.C. § 141; Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure

description: Semicolon-delimited list of patent numbers (e.g., US9,123,456; US10,234,567) asserted or challenged in this litigation. These are the Orange Book-listed or Blue Book-listed patents at issue. Links to the patent portfolio for expiry and claim analysis.
reference: 21 CFR Part 314.53; 35 U.S.C. § 271(e)(2); Orange Book (FDA Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations)

description: Free-text field for internal legal team notes, strategic observations, and case-specific commentary. May include attorney work product summaries, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations. Classified as confidential due to potential attorney-client privilege content.
reference: Attorney-Client Privilege; Federal Rules of Evidence Rule 502; GDPR Article 5

description: Official court-assigned or tribunal-assigned docket number uniquely identifying the litigation case (e.g., civil action number, IPR petition number, PGR petition number). Serves as the primary external business identifier for cross-referencing with legal counsel and court records.
reference: USPTO Rules of Practice; 35 U.S.C. § 311 (IPR); 35 U.S.C. § 321 (PGR); 21 CFR Part 314.53

description: Internal priority classification assigned to the litigation case based on revenue at risk, strategic importance, and likelihood of adverse outcome. Critical cases receive executive-level oversight; high cases are monitored by senior IP counsel; medium and low cases follow standard legal management processes.

Classification of the litigation case by legal mechanism. Paragraph IV ANDA challenges arise under Hatch-Waxman; IPR and PGR are USPTO trial proceedings; patent infringement suits are district court actions; declaratory judgment actions are filed by generic/biosimilar challengers; biosimilar patent dance refers to BPCIA exchange proceedings. reference: 35 U.S.C. §§ 271, 311, 321; 21 CFR Part 314.53; Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act (BPCIA)

description: Name of the judicial or administrative body presiding over the case (e.g., U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, USPTO Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, European Patent Office Opposition Division).
reference: 35 U.S.C. §§ 141, 311; USPTO Trial Practice Guide; EPC Article 99

description: Timestamp when this patent litigation record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 (Electronic Records); SOX Section 302; GDPR Article 5

description: Management's best estimate of the potential financial exposure or liability associated with this litigation case, expressed in US dollars. Used for legal reserve provisioning, financial disclosure under ASC 450 (contingencies), and SOX compliance. Includes potential damages, lost profits, and legal costs.
reference: ASC 450 (Contingencies); SOX Section 302; IAS 37 (Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets)

description: Date on which the complaint, petition, or challenge was formally filed with the court or tribunal. For Paragraph IV ANDA challenges, this is the date the ANDA filer notified the NDA holder. Critical for calculating the 30-month stay period and litigation timelines.

Indicates whether the ANDA challenger is the first filer entitled to 180-day generic exclusivity under the Hatch-Waxman Act. True if the defendant holds first-filer status; False otherwise. Relevant for assessing the competitive landscape and timing of generic entry.
reference: 21 U.S.C. § 355(j)(5)(B)(iv); Hatch-Waxman Act; FDA Orange Book

description: Date on which the PTAB issued its decision on whether to institute the IPR or PGR trial. A decision to institute means the petition met the threshold for review. Null for non-PTAB proceedings.
USPTO-assigned petition number for Inter Partes Review proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB). Format follows USPTO convention (e.g., IPR2023-01234). Null for non-IPR case types.
reference: 35 U.S.C. § 311; 37 CFR Part 42; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

description: Date on which the court or tribunal issued its final judgment, final written decision (for PTAB proceedings), or order. Null if the case has not yet reached judgment.
reference: 35 U.S.C. §§ 318, 328; Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 58

description: Full name of the lead attorney at the outside counsel firm responsible for managing this litigation matter. Used for escalation, communication, and legal budget accountability.
reference: SOX Section 302; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

description: Approved annual or total budget allocated for legal fees and costs associated with this litigation matter, expressed in US dollars. Used for variance analysis against actual legal spend and budget reforecasting.
reference: ASC 450; SOX Section 302; SAP S/4HANA CO Module

description: Current procedural status of the litigation case reflecting its lifecycle stage. Active cases are ongoing; settled cases have reached agreement; dismissed cases were terminated without judgment; judgment_entered reflects a court ruling; appealed cases are under appellate review; stayed cases are paused pending other proceedings; closed cases are fully resolved. reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

description: Description of the next significant procedural or substantive milestone in the litigation (e.g., claim construction hearing, expert discovery deadline, summary judgment motion, PTAB oral argument, appellate briefing deadline). Used for litigation calendar management.
reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

description: Scheduled date for the next key procedural or substantive milestone in the litigation. Used for proactive legal calendar management and escalation triggers.
reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

description: Final outcome or resolution of the litigation case. Patent upheld means the challenged patent survived; patent invalidated means the patent was found invalid or unenforceable; infringement found or non-infringement found reflects district court rulings; settled indicates out-of-court resolution; dismissed indicates termination without merits ruling; consent judgment reflects agreed court order. description: Name of the external law firm engaged to represent the company in this litigation matter. Used for legal spend tracking, conflict-of-interest management, and outside counsel performance evaluation.
reference: SOX Section 302 (legal contingency disclosure); GDPR Article 28 (data processor agreements with counsel)

description: Date on which the company received the formal Paragraph IV certification notice from the ANDA filer, as required under the Hatch-Waxman Act. Triggers the 45-day window to file suit and the 30-month stay. Null for non-Paragraph IV case types.

Legal name of the party initiating the litigation (typically the innovator/NDA holder asserting patent rights, or the generic/biosimilar applicant filing a declaratory judgment action). May be the company itself or a subsidiary.
reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 10; 21 CFR Part 314.53

description: Estimated annual revenue at risk if the litigation outcome is unfavorable and generic or biosimilar entry occurs earlier than the patent expiry date. Expressed in US dollars. Critical input for lifecycle management decisions and commercial strategy.
reference: ASC 450; SOX Section 302; ICH Q10 (lifecycle management)

description: Date on which a settlement agreement was executed between the parties, if the case was resolved through settlement rather than judgment. Null for cases resolved by judgment or still active.
reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 41; FTC Act (reverse payment settlement scrutiny); 21 CFR Part 314

description: Agreed date on which the generic or biosimilar entrant is permitted to launch its product under the terms of the settlement agreement. Critical for lifecycle management and revenue forecasting. Null for non-settlement outcomes.
reference: Hatch-Waxman Act; FTC Act; 21 CFR Part 314.53

description: Date on which the NDA holder filed the patent infringement suit in response to the Paragraph IV notice, within the 45-day statutory window. Null for case types where the company is the defendant or for non-Hatch-Waxman proceedings.

Therapeutic area or disease category associated with the drug product at the center of the litigation (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neuroscience). Enables portfolio-level analysis of litigation exposure by therapeutic area.
reference: ATC Classification System (WHO); ICH E6 (GCP); FDA Therapeutic Area Guidance

description: Date on which the automatic 30-month stay of FDA approval of the ANDA expires under the Hatch-Waxman Act. Calculated from the date the NDA holder received the Paragraph IV certification notice. Null for non-Hatch-Waxman case types. Critical for generic entry defense strategy.

Scheduled or actual date of the trial or oral hearing before the court or tribunal. For PTAB proceedings, this is the oral argument date. Null if trial has not been scheduled or the case settled prior to trial.
reference: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure; USPTO Trial Practice Guide

The functional area classification for cost-of-sales accounting. Represents business functions such as R&D, manufacturing, sales, marketing, or administration.
The primary geographic region or market that this profit center serves. Used for regional P&L reporting and market access strategy.
The node identifier in the profit center standard hierarchy. Enables roll-up reporting and aggregation of P&L across organizational structures (e.g., by therapeutic area, geography, or product line).
The primary language code for profit center descriptions and reporting. Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., EN, DE, FR).

The user ID of the person who last modified this profit center master record. Used for change tracking and data stewardship accountability.

description: The date and time when this profit center master record was last modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and compliance requirements.

description: The product line or portfolio grouping associated with this profit center. May represent a brand family, drug class, or commercial franchise.
The business identifier code for the profit center as defined in SAP Controlling. Typically alphanumeric, 4-10 characters. Used across financial reporting, P&L statements, and management accounting.
The full business name or description of the profit center. Human-readable label used in financial reports and management dashboards.

The current lifecycle status of the profit center. Active profit centers are operational and accept postings. Planned profit centers are set up but not yet operational. Closed profit centers are historical and no longer accept postings.

description: Unique identifier for the system crosswalk mapping record. Primary key for the cross-system identifier mapping table.
Identifier of the data steward responsible for approving and maintaining this identifier mapping. Used for data governance accountability and audit trail.
Reference to the business rule or transformation logic used to establish this identifier mapping. Links to MDM governance documentation and mapping specifications.
Reference to the specific merger, acquisition, or divestiture event that triggered the creation of this identifier mapping. Null for mappings created during normal operations.

Numeric score (0.00 to 100.00) representing the confidence level in the accuracy of this identifier mapping. Higher scores indicate greater certainty in the mapping relationship. Used for data quality management and reconciliation prioritization.
User identifier of the person or system process that created this identifier mapping record. Required for audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
Timestamp when this identifier mapping record was first created in the system. Required for audit trail and regulatory compliance.
Date after which this identifier mapping is no longer valid. Null indicates the mapping is currently active with no planned expiration.
Date from which this identifier mapping becomes valid and should be used for cross-system integration and Master Data Management (MDM) golden record resolution.
Type of master data entity being mapped across systems. Indicates whether the mapping is for materials, business partners, sites, compounds, organizational units, or products.
Indicates whether this mapping represents the authoritative Master Data Management (MDM) golden record relationship for this entity. True for the primary system-of-record mapping.

Indicates whether this identifier mapping is subject to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), or Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulatory requirements. True for mappings involving regulated master data.
User identifier of the person or system process that most recently modified this identifier mapping record. Required for audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
Timestamp when this identifier mapping record was most recently modified. Required for audit trail and regulatory compliance.
Timestamp of the most recent reconciliation process that validated this identifier mapping against source and target systems. Used for audit trail and data quality monitoring.
Indicates whether the mapping is unidirectional (source to target only) or bidirectional (can be used in both directions for identifier resolution).
Method by which the identifier mapping was established. Manual indicates data steward creation; automated indicates system-generated; ML-derived indicates machine learning algorithm output.
Free-text field for data stewards to document special considerations, exceptions, or context about this identifier mapping. Used for knowledge transfer and troubleshooting.

Current lifecycle status of the identifier mapping. Active mappings are used for integration; deprecated mappings are retained for historical audit; pending validation mappings await data steward approval.
Indicates whether this identifier mapping was created as part of a merger, acquisition, or divestiture data harmonization effort. True for M&A-related mappings requiring special governance.
Result of the most recent reconciliation check. Matched indicates both identifiers exist and are consistent; mismatch indicates data quality issue requiring investigation.
Human-readable description or name of the entity as it appears in the source system. Aids in manual validation and troubleshooting of identifier mappings.
The identifier value as it exists in the source system. This is the original identifier that needs to be mapped to the target system.
Code identifying the source system from which the identifier originates. Examples: SAP_S4, VEEVA_VAULT, LIMS_LABWARE, ARGUS, MEDIDATA, MES, VEEVA_CRM.
Specific instance or environment of the source system (e.g., production, quality assurance, development). Important for multi-instance SAP S/4HANA or Veeva Vault deployments.

Indicates whether this identifier mapping is relevant for Sarbanes-Oxley Act financial reporting compliance. True for mappings involving financial master data such as cost centers, profit centers, or general ledger accounts.
Human-readable description or name of the entity as it appears in the target system. Aids in manual validation and troubleshooting of identifier mappings.
The corresponding identifier value in the target system. This is the mapped identifier that the source identifier resolves to.
Code identifying the target system to which the identifier is mapped. Examples: SAP_S4, VEEVA_VAULT, LIMS_LABWARE, ARGUS, MEDIDATA, MES, VEEVA_CRM.
Specific instance or environment of the target system (e.g., production, quality assurance, development). Important for multi-instance SAP S/4HANA or Veeva Vault deployments.
Timestamp when this identifier mapping was last validated or approved by a data steward. Critical for regulatory compliance and data quality assurance.
Unique identifier for the material plant data record. Primary key.

business_glossary_term: Material Plant Data - Masterdata Material Master Id
description: Foreign key linking to the material master record for which plant-specific parameters are defined.
Foreign key linking to the plant facility where the material-specific operational parameters apply.

ABC classification of the material at this plant based on consumption value or strategic importance. A=High value/critical, B=Medium value/importance, C=Low value/routine. Used for inventory control prioritization.
Timestamp when this material plant data record was first created in the system.
Timestamp when this material plant data record was last updated, used for change tracking and data synchronization.

Lot-sizing procedure that determines how order quantities are calculated during MRP runs. EX=Lot-for-lot, FX=Fixed lot size, HB=Replenishment to maximum stock, LZ=Economic order quantity, WB=Weekly lot size.
Material Requirements Planning procedure type that determines how the material is planned at this plant. PD=MRP, VB=Manual reorder point, VM=Forecast-based, VV=Reorder point planning, ND=No planning.
Plant-specific material identifier that may differ from the enterprise material number, used for local operations and legacy system integration.
Indicates how the material is procured at this specific plant. E=External procurement (purchased), F=In-house production (manufactured), X=Both external and in-house.
Identifier or name of the production scheduler or planner responsible for this material at this plant, used for MRP exception management and planning coordination.
Quality management inspection group code that defines which QC laboratory team is responsible for testing this material at this plant, linking to quality inspection procedures.
Inventory level at which a procurement or production order should be triggered for this material at this plant, expressed in the material base unit of measure.
Minimum inventory quantity that must be maintained at this plant to buffer against demand variability and supply disruptions, expressed in the material base unit of measure.
Default storage location code within the plant where this material is typically stored, used for automatic goods receipt and inventory management.
Date from which this material plant data record is effective and should be used for planning and operations at this plant.
Date until which this material plant data record is effective. Null indicates the record is currently active with no planned end date.
Unique identifier for this material-storage location configuration record. Primary key.

business_glossary_term: Material Storage Location Data - Masterdata Material Master Id
description: Foreign key linking to the material master record

business_glossary_term: Material Storage Location Data - Storage Location Id
description: Foreign key linking to the storage location master record
Flag indicating whether batch-level tracking is required for this material at this storage location. May differ from material master if location-specific requirements apply.
Specific bin or shelf location within the storage location where this material is stored. Used for picking and putaway operations.
Timestamp when this material-storage location configuration record was first created in the system.
Hazardous material storage classification for this material at this storage location. Ensures segregation and compliance with OSHA/DOT requirements.
Timestamp when this material-storage location configuration record was last modified.
Maximum inventory level allowed for this material at this storage location. Prevents overstocking and ensures capacity compliance.
Minimum inventory level to maintain for this material at this storage location. Safety stock requirement.
Designated picking zone within the storage location for this material. Optimizes warehouse operations and order fulfillment.
Warehouse management strategy for placing incoming goods of this material into this storage location. Examples: FIFO, FEFO, fixed bin, bulk storage.
Inventory level at which replenishment should be triggered for this material at this storage location. Used for automated procurement planning.
Classification of the bin type used for this material at this storage location. Examples: pallet rack, shelf, bulk bin, cold storage bin.
Flag indicating whether continuous temperature monitoring is required for this material at this storage location. Critical for cold-chain integrity and regulatory compliance.
Date from which this material-storage location configuration becomes effective. Supports time-dependent storage configurations.
Date until which this material-storage location configuration remains effective. Null indicates indefinite validity.

description: City or municipality where the plant facility is located.

Primary cost center code assigned to the plant facility for cost accounting and financial controlling purposes.

DEA registration number for facilities handling controlled substances, required for manufacturing, distribution, or research involving scheduled drugs.
Unique site identifier assigned by the European Medicines Agency for manufacturing and testing facilities within the European Economic Area.

Current status of environmental operating permits required for pharmaceutical manufacturing operations at the plant facility.

Geographic longitude coordinate of the plant facility in decimal degrees, used for logistics planning and geographic analysis.
Name and version of the Manufacturing Execution System used at the plant for batch execution, electronic batch records, and production tracking.
reference: ISA-95 Enterprise-Control System Integration, 21 CFR Part 11

Primary contact telephone number for the plant facility including country and area codes.
Business identifier code for the plant facility, typically used in SAP S/4HANA and other operational systems for cross-system reference.
Full business name of the plant facility as registered with regulatory authorities and used in official documentation.

Postal or ZIP code for the plant facility address used for mail delivery and geographic reference.
Name and version of the Quality Management System software platform used at the plant (e.g., MasterControl, TrackWise, Veeva Vault QualityDocs).

First line of the physical address for this storage location. Includes building number, street name, and suite/unit if applicable. Required for GDP traceability and regulatory inspections.

description: Second line of the physical address for this storage location. Optional field for additional address details such as building name or department.
reference: GDP Guidelines PIC/S, SAP S/4HANA MM Plant Master

description: Unit of measure for the capacity_storage_units field. Standardizes capacity reporting across heterogeneous storage types.

description: City where this storage location is physically located. Required for regulatory reporting and distribution planning.
reference: GDP Guidelines PIC/S, SAP S/4HANA MM Plant Master

description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the storage location. Examples: USA, GBR, DEU, JPN, CHN. Required for multi-country regulatory reporting and GDP compliance.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Country Codes, GDP Guidelines PIC/S

description: Timestamp when this storage location master record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data governance and compliance.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records, GDPR Article 5 Data Integrity

description: DEA registration number for storage locations authorized to hold controlled substances (Schedule II-V). Format: 2 letters + 7 digits. Required for controlled substance accountability and regulatory inspections. Null for non-controlled substance storage.

description: Highest DEA controlled substance schedule this storage location is authorized to hold. Schedule II requires vault-level security. Not applicable for non-controlled substance storage.
reference: 21 CFR Part 1301 DEA Registration, 21 CFR Part 1304 Records and Reports

description: Date when this storage location was decommissioned or permanently closed. Null for active storage locations. Used for historical reporting and audit trail.
reference: SAP S/4HANA WM Storage Location Master

description: Date when this storage location became operational and available for goods movements. Marks the beginning of the storage locations lifecycle in the master data system.
reference: SAP S/4HANA WM Storage Location Master

description: Indicates whether this storage location meets GDP requirements for pharmaceutical distribution. True for qualified distribution centers with temperature mapping, security, and traceability controls. False for non-GDP locations.
reference: GDP Guidelines PIC/S, EU GDP Guidelines 2013/C 343/01

description: Cleanroom classification per EU GMP Annex 1 or ISO 14644. Grade A for aseptic processing, Grade D for general manufacturing. Unclassified for non-GMP warehouses. Drives gowning, environmental monitoring, and personnel flow requirements.
reference: EU GMP Annex 1 Manufacture of Sterile Medicinal Products, ISO 14644 Cleanroom Standards

description: Classification of hazardous materials authorized for storage per OSHA and DOT regulations. Determines segregation requirements, fire suppression systems, and emergency response protocols. Non-hazardous for general storage.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106 Flammable Liquids, DOT 49 CFR Part 172 Hazardous Materials Table

description: Maximum allowable relative humidity percentage for this storage location. Excursions may impact product stability and require OOT investigation. Null if humidity control is not required.

description: Minimum allowable relative humidity percentage for this storage location. Required for hygroscopic API and moisture-sensitive drug products. Null if humidity control is not required.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability Testing, 21 CFR Part 211.142 Warehousing Procedures

description: Timestamp when this storage location master record was last updated. Tracks change history for audit trail and data stewardship.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records, GDPR Article 5 Data Integrity

description: Date of the most recent qualification or requalification of this storage location per CSV and GMP requirements. Includes temperature mapping, humidity validation, and security system testing. Drives requalification scheduling.
reference: GAMP 5 CSV Guidelines, ICH Q7 GMP for APIs, 21 CFR Part 211 GMP Requirements

description: Scheduled date for the next periodic requalification of this storage location. Typically annual or biennial based on risk assessment. Overdue qualifications may trigger storage location blocking.
reference: GAMP 5 CSV Guidelines, ICH Q7 GMP for APIs

description: Postal or ZIP code for this storage location. Required for logistics planning and regulatory correspondence.
reference: GDP Guidelines PIC/S, SAP S/4HANA MM Plant Master

description: Indicates whether this storage location is designated as a quarantine zone for materials pending QC release, under investigation, or rejected. True for quarantine areas, false for released goods storage.
reference: 21 CFR Part 211.80 General Requirements for Components, ICH Q7 GMP for APIs

description: Indicates whether this storage location is designated for processing returned goods, including customer returns, expired products, and recalls. True for returns processing areas requiring segregation and disposition workflows.
reference: 21 CFR Part 211.204 Returned Drug Products, GDP Guidelines PIC/S

description: Indicates whether this storage location is designated for QC sampling activities. True for sampling areas where materials are temporarily held for sample collection per sampling plans.
reference: 21 CFR Part 211.84 Testing and Approval or Rejection of Components

description: Physical security classification for this storage location. High for DEA vaults and high-value products requiring 24/7 surveillance, access control, and intrusion detection. Medium for controlled access areas. Standard for general warehouses.
reference: 21 CFR Part 1301.71 DEA Security Requirements, GDP Guidelines PIC/S

description: Indicates whether materials in this storage location must be physically segregated from other materials due to cross-contamination risk, regulatory requirements, or product incompatibility. True for quarantine zones, controlled substances, and hazmat.
reference: 21 CFR Part 211.176 Penicillin Contamination, ICH Q7 GMP for APIs

description: State or province where this storage location is physically located. Required for state-level regulatory reporting and DEA registration.
reference: GDP Guidelines PIC/S, 21 CFR Part 1301 DEA Registration

description: Business identifier for the storage location. Alphanumeric code used across SAP WM, LIMS, and MES systems for warehouse management and batch traceability. Typically 4-10 characters.
reference: SAP S/4HANA WM Storage Location Master

description: Human-readable name of the storage location. Examples: Cold Room 2-8C Building A, DEA Vault Schedule II, Quarantine Zone QC Lab 3, Hazmat Storage Flammables.
reference: SAP S/4HANA WM Storage Location Master

description: Current operational status of the storage location. Blocked status prevents goods movements pending CAPA resolution or requalification. Under qualification indicates validation in progress per CSV requirements.

reference: ICH Q1A Stability Testing, GDP Guidelines PIC/S

reference: ICH Q1A Stability Testing, GDP Guidelines PIC/S

description: Type of temperature monitoring system deployed at this storage location. Continuous automated systems provide real-time alerts for excursions. Periodic manual monitoring uses data loggers with batch review. Not monitored for ambient storage.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability Testing, GDP Guidelines PIC/S, 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records

description: Indicates whether this storage location is integrated with a WMS for automated goods movements, bin management, and real-time inventory tracking. True for WMS-managed locations, false for manual locations.

Identifier of the data steward or data owner responsible for maintaining the accuracy and quality of this address record. Used for data governance, accountability, and escalation of data quality issues.

Current lifecycle status of the address record. Active addresses are currently in use, inactive addresses are no longer valid but retained for historical reference, pending addresses are awaiting approval or validation, and archived addresses are historical records retained for compliance.

Classification of the address purpose within pharmaceutical operations. description: City or municipality name where the address is located. Used for geographic segmentation, logistics planning, and regulatory reporting by jurisdiction.
reference: ISO 19160-1; Universal Postal Union S42 Standard

description: Timestamp when this address record was first created in the master data system. Used for audit trail, data lineage tracking, and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.

Nine-digit Dun & Bradstreet DUNS number uniquely identifying the business entity at this address. Used for vendor qualification, supply chain due diligence, and compliance with pharmaceutical procurement standards.

Date when this address ceased to be valid or was replaced by a new address. Null for currently active addresses. Used for historical reporting and compliance with Good Documentation Practice (GDP) requirements.
Date when this address became valid and active for business use. Used for temporal tracking of address changes, critical for audit trails and regulatory inspection history.

Primary email contact for the address location. Used for electronic communication, document transmission, and coordination with Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMO), Contract Research Organizations (CRO), and regulatory authorities.

Fax number for the address location. Still used in pharmaceutical industry for transmitting regulatory documents, Certificates of Analysis (CoA), and Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) documentation where electronic signatures are not yet implemented.

Boolean indicator identifying whether the address location holds current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) certification. True indicates the site is certified for pharmaceutical manufacturing under FDA, EMA, or other regulatory authority standards.
reference: 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211; EMA GMP Guidelines; ICH Q7

description: Two-letter ISO language code indicating the primary language used at this address location. Used for generating localized documentation, labeling, and communication in compliance with regional regulatory requirements.

Timestamp of the most recent update to this address record. Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and ensuring compliance with Good Documentation Practice (GDP) requirements for maintaining current and accurate master data.

Geographic latitude coordinate in decimal degrees format. Used for geospatial analytics, supply chain route optimization, clinical trial site mapping, and emergency response planning for manufacturing facilities.
Primary street address line containing street number, street name, and building identifier. This is the main address component used for physical location identification and postal delivery.

description: Secondary address line for additional location details such as suite number, floor, building name, department, or unit identifier. Optional field used when address_line_1 is insufficient for precise location identification.

description: Tertiary address line for complex addresses requiring additional location context such as industrial park name, campus identifier, or district information. Rarely used but necessary for large pharmaceutical manufacturing complexes or research campuses.
reference: Universal Postal Union S42 Standard; ISO 19160-1

description: Geographic longitude coordinate in decimal degrees format. Used in conjunction with latitude for precise geolocation, distribution center proximity analysis, and cold chain logistics planning.
